For each later input record: stable ID, exact reference and locator, full
statement, coefficient and degree dependence, quantifier order, uniformity,
Lean type, uses, and status (`proved`, `mathlib`, `explicit_hypothesis`, or
`unresolved`). Include the exact upstream commit for Mathlib results.

If a literature result is intentionally left unformalized, pass it as an
ordinary explicit theorem argument and state that conditional scope in the
coverage and Palomar metadata. Do not introduce a global `axiom`, and do not
describe a theorem conditional on an external estimate as having proved it.

Start with the cited sources behind the split-product, quadratic-equation,
determinant and local rigidity bounds in companion T1 and article Section 2.
Compare the stronger uniformity required here with the exact interfaces in
Paper C; importing an old interface alone cannot discharge this comparison.

## Fixed-window exposure and full-vector independence

Stable ID: `P1-ARITH-FIXED-WINDOW-BRANCHING`. Status: **proved**, complete T1.15.

- The entire actual new relative vector has its fair product law and
  Mathlib `IndepFun` from all old raw values whenever its supported-value
  count is at most one. Every conditional word mass and the literal
  joint pushforward are proved; unrealizable old vectors have zero mass.
- Finite prime-cardinality and positive-integer reciprocal-half-power
  bounds prove the source explicit rounded exceptional estimate. A
  smaller deterministic set removes the contact term and halves the
  pool coefficient, as recorded in P1-MATH-0030. The actual critical
  prime-pool count proves the uniform fixed-j exponent.
- No independence, conditional word law, prime-cardinality, Euler or
  exceptional-count estimate is assumed. Injective complete-boundary
  embeddings and transposes prove the exact laws of all selected subsets
  and fitted positive fixed dilations. Arbitrary bounded old observations,
  fixed enlarged logarithmic widths, positive height multiples and
  injective center reindexings are included, with thresholds before all
  such choices. No additional Paper C source or unproved literature
  statement is introduced. See
  [alignment](FIXED_BRANCHING_ALIGNMENT.md).

Stable ID: `P1-ARITH-PNT`. Status: **proved**.

`primeCount B ≤ (1+η) * B / log B`. The sequential limit

`PaperP1.SharpPrimeCount.primeCount_upper_eventually` and
`PaperP1.SharpPrimeCount.prime_counting_ratio_tendsto`.

*A formally verified proof of the prime number theorem*, ACM TOCL 9(1),
Article 2 (2007), DOI
[10.1145/1297658.1297660](https://doi.org/10.1145/1297658.1297660),
[preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0509025), introduction, page 1.

## Actual retained-error convergence from finitely many fixed primitive orders

Stable ID: `P1-PROB-VANISHING-RETAINED-ERROR-BCN`. Status: **proved conditional on the existing explicit BCN bound**.

Here delta is the literal probability that the actual active configuration is
not retained. No estimate for delta or convergence assertion is a premise.

The finite probabilistic step is unconditional: a nonretained active set has
positive relative nullity and hence contains an actual minimally dependent
subfamily of size at least two. For every finite cutoff K,

    delta <= actualMean/(K+1)
             + sum_(r=2..K) actualJointMass(primitiveFamilies of size r).

The expectation identity uses the exact finite cylinder of the original
infinite measure. The first term handles configurations with more than K
active starts; the remaining terms are actual joint probabilities, not
centered activities or formal weights. Empty ground sets and zero marginals
are included.

Under BCN, the two-site primitive joint mass is at most N^(-1/2+eta), using
the actual pair host count and actual joint-probability bound. Every fixed
order r>=3 has this same weaker bound from the unconditional primitive
estimate N^(1-r/2+eta). Only finitely many fixed orders are assembled.
The critical actual mean is uniformly bounded by M=2*2^C. Choose K after
epsilon so that M/(K+1)<=epsilon/2, then choose N0 to make the finitely many
primitive masses sum to at most epsilon/2. In particular K is fixed before
N, and no fixed-order constant is applied to an order growing with N.

This proves qualitative disappearance of the actual modification and its
coupling error. It does not prove the source rate N^(-4/5+eta), identify the

       <= ||x||^k * exp(||x||) / k!.

It is proved from the actual exponential series and the divisibility of
j!*k! into (j+k)!, not assumed as an interface. Applied in the completed
ordinary-l1 convolution algebra to x=mu*Delta, it bounds the Poisson
remainder by (2*mu)^k*exp(2*mu)/k!. Singleton coefficient comparison
transports the completed-norm bound to actual total variation. Universal
Poisson parameter stability TV(Pois(mu),Pois(nu))<=|mu-nu| is proved too.

factorial tails for this fixed M are small. Only then assemble the

moment of order k is bounded by mu_N^k+1, and the finite polynomial error

convergent exponential series makes the reconstruction tails vanish.

## P1-PROB-HOMOGENEOUS-SEED-MASS

Internal affine rank-nullity, actual zero-target cylinders, private exact units and existing fixed-source probability propagation; no new external input.

The homogeneous zero-target window event is now defined under the
actual infinite prime-sign measure. For positive L, its relative bit
prescription is proved equivalent to equality of the value signs at
x-1, x, ..., x+L-1. For any finite family I, its joint probability is
exactly 2^(-rank of the sum of its actual square-class spaces), and is
strictly positive. Tuple support transport includes repetitions and the
empty family. The probability is antitone under adding windows.

For every I contained in the regular dyadic set, this actual homogeneous
probability equals the source weight

    W(I) = p^|I| 2^(rho(I)), p=2^(-L).

The exact rank-nullity identity proves this equality. It is not asserted
with nominal marginals on irregular sites. The actual original run joint
probability is at most the homogeneous probability for every finite I
and every positive L, including irregular and incompatible families.

In a raw private good channel a:b, every pair has homogeneous mass
p^2 2^(u-1), where u is its exact-unit count. This has no affine
compatibility restriction. For each fixed coprime 0<a<b, its total
unordered homogeneous mass is at most K_(C,a,b) L N^(-1+1/b), uniformly
over the private-prime cutoff H and all sufficiently large critical N,L.
The raw principal family is the union of the 2:3 and 3:4 raw good pairs.
Its W mass is bounded above by K_C L N^(-2/3) for every H and below by
c_(C,D) L N^(-2/3) when 8(L+1)<=H<=D(L+1). The lower bound follows from
the actual compatible principal beta mass, which is at most this raw
homogeneous mass. No cancellation or compatibility filter is used in
the upper bound. This proves the principal raw seed scale stated in
the moreover clause of the first part of T1.12.

For fixed positive seed size s and fixed extension size k, the sum of
actual homogeneous probabilities over any unordered family of size
s+k containing a seed is bounded by (s+k)! N^epsilon times the sum of
the seed probabilities. All seed and target populations vary after
the same threshold. On regular populations this transports exactly
to W mass. Consequently, for every fixed r, the sum of W over all
r-subsets of any regular dyadic subfamily is at most N^epsilon.
These statements are unconditional and concern fixed orders only.

forces

strengthening the source constants 24 and 72. The existing uniform

## P1-DIOPH-POLYNOMIAL-MOVING-ROOT-COUNT

Internal positive quadratic counts, squarefree kernels, offset resultants and elementary divisor subpolynomiality; no new external input.

The one-variable split-product count now permits arbitrary moving
integer offsets. For fixed natural K,d and epsilon>0, one threshold
precedes every offset set A, nonzero integer coefficient c and finite
solution population S. If 2<=|A|<=d, every actual value n+a is positive
and at most N^K, and

    c * product_(a in A)(n+a) is an integer square,

then |S|<=N^epsilon. The variable n is natural but has no required
comparison with N. The offsets can be arbitrarily far from zero;
only the actual positive values are bounded. The coefficient c has
no height restriction. Two equations with disjoint nonempty offset
sets satisfy the same count. Fixed product-kernel fibres also have
the same bound, uniformly in their squarefree kernel.

The argument is internal. Two fixed individual squarefree kernels give
an injective positive Pell representation, with coefficients, square
parts and offset difference bounded by N^K. The full product kernel
and pairwise offset resultant have height at most N^(K(d+d^2)), using
one actual solution and the positive value cap. Individual prime
supports lie in that fixed kernel-resultant support. The number of
support codes is at most 4^omega(m)<=tau(m)^2=N^o(1), and every code
fibre is bounded by the checked uniform positive quadratic theorem.
Both square and nonsquare coefficient ratios are included.

This strengthens the previously checked one-variable portions of T1.7
and T4.1 beyond logarithmic offset windows, without Pila or another
external curve-counting premise. It provides an input for moving line
substitutions in later planar arguments; those substitutions and the

## Covered residual host counts and exact packing

The prescribed-plane and unrestricted host assertions of T20.8 are
proved on the actual covered three-window relation space. For each
arbitrary cover, its unpinned components meeting all three blocks give
an exact finite family of pairwise disjoint transverse motifs. Their
natural products equal the component products used by T20.7, so their
small-prime square constraints are literal. Component-to-vertex-set
injectivity preserves their exact count. The finite small-prime rank
cost is uniformly below any fixed fraction of B.

Consequently, if any cover has residual dimension at least eta*L,
then the triple admits at least (eta/4)*B actual disjoint transverse
square products, eventually and uniformly in all covers. T20.6 then
gives N^(1+epsilon) hosts and N^(-1+epsilon) original affine mass on
every prescribed polynomial family of integer planes. The cover stays
inside an existential host predicate and is never enumerated. The
bound holds before primitive filtering, and hence for the literal
primitive mass as well. The real cutoff H=C0*B is retained exactly.

The unrestricted N^(3/2+epsilon) count of primitive triples is also
proved. In fact it follows from the stronger elementary fixed-order
count of all primitive hosts, without a residual-dimension premise.
A new exact finite conversion from unordered families to injective
center functions supplies the r! enumeration factor and works at
every fixed r>=2. It preserves the original primitive predicate.

The six-vertex packing calculation itself is now exact and checked:
6*dim(R_D)+|D| <= 3B+3*s(D)+18*(pi(H)+2), where s(D) is the literal
number of free transverse components of size at most five. Its real
form gives (3B-|D|)/6+s(D)/2+3*(pi(H)+2). This includes arbitrary
covers and pins. The remaining unproved part of T20.8 is the exceptional
mass N^(-1+epsilon) needed to bound s(D) by a fixed constant simultaneously
for every cover. That small-component exclusion still needs the
unrestricted degree-one geometric count. It is not inferred from
packing or from the planar proposition.

## P1-ACTUAL-PRIVATE-RATIONAL-GAP

Internal finite intersection arithmetic, the checked rational extremal gap, exact affine witnesses and critical binary powers. No new external input.

The actual private zero-intercept rational sector of main 14.3 is
proved, uniformly at polynomial logarithmic slope height. For primitive
0<u<v<w<2u and t>=1, use product normalizers (v*w,u*w,u*v) on the
actual centers (u*t,v*t,w*t). A private normalized union implies actual
affine compatibility: its predecessors lie below their common origin
and every internal value lies at or above it. No affine positivity
surrogate is assumed.

Common integer dilation preserves exact intersection cardinalities.
Reducing each physical ratio gives pair intersection bounds
B*gcd(u,v)/v+1, B*gcd(u,w)/w+1 and B*gcd(v,w)/w+1.
The actual triple intersection contains all origin+u*v*w*m for
0<=m<=floor((L-1)/w); only this lower bound is needed. Exact three-set
inclusion-exclusion then proves that 3L-(union.card-1) is at most
D(u,v,w)*L+5. Thus the actual effective rank is at least
(71/30)*L-5, and it is at least (43/18)*L-5 away from the unique
extremal physical triple (10,12,15).

These are finite uniform bounds with no slope-height restriction.
They give original affine probability at most
2^(5+(71/30)*C)*N^(-71/30), or
2^(5+(43/18)*C)*N^(-43/18) in the nonextremal sector.
The existing sharp geometric gap P1-MATH-0067 therefore becomes an
actual probability gap on these private normalized triples.

## Full even rank and common normalization invariance

The finite normalized-family criterion P1-MATH-0098 is strengthened:
injectivity on even selections of the normalized union suffices. Full
raw private-prime independence is unnecessary. A finite embedding
extension proves restriction to every subfamily, and rank-nullity
identifies the new condition with exact even-image rank union.card-1.
The literal set {1,2} proves the weakening is strict: its even map is
injective although the square value 1 has no private prime.

Any requested relative value bits are realized by an actual infinite
prime-sign sample, up to one common bit. That bit cancels in all run
constraints, giving actual affine compatibility whenever no normalized
predecessor equals a normalized internal value. Exact local ranks,
joint rank and actual infinite-model joint probability follow. A common
normalized value or, more generally, connected normalized overlap gives
rank union.card-1 and probability 2^(-(union.card-1)). Both versions
retain the exact p^r*2^rho formula with its literal dimension equation.

The new even-injectivity criterion, predecessor exclusivity and union
cardinality are invariant under every common positive integer dilation.
They therefore agree for any two positive normalization vectors with
a common positive rational ratio. There is no restriction on the prime
factors or height of the common factors. This removes a dependence on
the normalization choice that raw private-value independence does not
share.

For primitive zero-intercept rational triples, all checked actual
probability and mass upper bounds now hold under this strictly weaker
even-rank condition: point exponents -71/30 and -43/18, and ordered or
unordered host mass exponents -41/30 and -25/18 at polynomial
logarithmic slope height. The original private host population is
proved contained in the new one and its actual mass is dominated.

large-prime kernel, which is supported on actual defective values of

O_Q(B/log B) bound and hence an arbitrarily small multiple of B.

Q is fixed before the threshold; these unconditional bounds do not
assert uniformity for Q growing as a power of B.

## Arbitrary affine positions and explicit canonical endpoint error

A finite divisibility proof makes the canonical-overlap endpoint
error explicit and covers arbitrary independent translations of the
three windows. For primitive u<v<w<2u, every L>=0 and every actual
center vector X with X_i>=2, let U be the union of the three complete
windows normalized by (v*w,u*w,u*v). The checked bound is

3L-(U.card-1) <= D(u,v,w)*L+3.

No geometric alignment, common normalized value, dyadic restriction,
private prime, even-rank injectivity or affine compatibility is needed
for this finite cardinality statement. It implies
U.card-1 >= (71/30)*L-3, and at least (43/18)*L-3 away from
(10,12,15). The absolute error 3 is uniform in all slope heights and
translations. The previous explicit zero-intercept specialization had
error 5; the manuscript itself stated an unspecified absolute O(1).

The proof counts the third window only once. All its coincidences
with the first two windows lie in the union of divisibility classes
w/gcd(u,w) and w/gcd(v,w). Their least common multiple is exactly w
by primitive normalization. Exact floor counts in an arbitrary
complete positive-integer window give upper errors 1,1 and a lower
error 1 for their intersection. Combining this union bound with the
first-pair count proves the finite loss bound, without requiring a
lower bound on the actual triple intersection. In particular, the
three pair-overlap locations need not coincide.

If the normalized intersection graph is connected and the union has
full even rank, this finite result yields actual affine joint
probability bounds with constants 2^(3+(71/30)*C) and
2^(3+(43/18)*C), retaining the original infinite prime-sign law and
all zero-probability incompatible systems. Predecessor exclusivity
is not required for these upper bounds. The asymptotic exponents and
the unique extremal physical triple are unchanged.

The aligned-target mass is now stated on literal dyadic three-element

assumed reduced affine representation. For a source channel in any
fixed finite reduced interior family F, a second geometric relation
|s*x-r*z| <= (r+s)*B supplies the required affine data. The proof
selects one actual x-window multiple of a, reduces the coefficient

compressed center X=a*b*t in a fixed enlarged width D*B. The existing
reduced-data construction supplies height B^5 inside the proof.
Its actual mass has the same N^(-41/30+epsilon) bound across F,
including zero-unit sources, physical ratios, endpoint populations,
local arithmetic defects and affine incompatibility. Source membership
and inclusion in the proved finite affine pool are checked separately.

## Actual ternary prime groups and center-independent forced planes

The finite arithmetic and plane-forcing core of companion T1.16
is now proved for actual prime groups on three arbitrary finite
sets of positive integers. This is the source ternary group
budget, not the separate abstract ternary selection theorem T2.3.
The final CRT tail sums and fixed-k induction are still open,
so T1.16 moves from not_started to in_progress, not proved.

TernaryPrimeGroups constructs the actual finite value-triple
pool and, for each triple, the product of exactly the primes
above H with odd valuation in all three entries. Membership,
primality, positivity, squarefreeness and divisibility of every
entry are proved. A prime above the common diameter cannot
occur at two different values in a block. Consequently the
prime sets of distinct actual triples are disjoint, their
products are coprime, and all active group values greater than
one are distinct. The strict decreasing-order convention in
the source therefore causes no hidden tie issue. The literal
support-pool cardinality is the product of the three set sizes.

The arithmetic rigidity is proved for arbitrary finite sets.
Injectivity of an even-selection map implies injectivity of
its data vectors, by the two-coordinate zero-sum selection.
For the finite forcing argument it suffices that the parity
vectors of distinct local values are distinct, together with
pairwise disjoint even square-class images. Proportional
positive value pairs would give the same nonzero even class
in two disjoint images, which is impossible. The three-block
projection rigidity is derived from these actual arithmetic
hypotheses; it is not an assumed geometric exclusion.

Actual products of two groups divide every corresponding
2x2 integer minor. If values are at most A and within-block
diameters are at most H, the minor is at most 2AH. A shared
value is handled separately using coprimality and product
divisibility. This gives the uniform finite bound 2A(H+1).
The product of three actual groups divides their 3x3 determinant,
whose absolute value is at most 6AH^2. A group product greater
than this threshold forces the determinant to vanish.

The collinear exception is excluded without a primitive-direction
choice. Put d=v-u for the first two value triples. If u,v,w
are collinear, d cross u=d cross v=d cross w. Every actual
group therefore divides all coordinates of the same integer
cross vector. Pairwise coprimality makes their product divide
it, while each coordinate is at most 2AH. A larger product
forces the cross vector to vanish. The actual pairwise
square-class rigidity then forces u=v, contradicting distinct
supports. Thus, for H>=1, product>6AH^2 forces a genuine plane.
Every normal coordinate is proved nonzero, using the actual
positive projection rigidity and the vanishing determinant.
This unconditional finite simplification and weaker local
hypothesis are recorded as P1-MATH-0114. It is not an assertion
of the still open asymptotic counting bound.

For centers X and offsets bounded in absolute value by R,
the normal is identified with the cross product of offset
differences; it is independent of a common center translation.
Each normal coordinate has absolute value at most 8R^2 and
the plane constant is at most 24R^3. The centers satisfy the
actual resulting integer-plane equation. The actual plane
belongs to an explicitly defined pool depending only on R,
of cardinality (16R^2+1)^3*(48R^3+1). The plane is genuine and
all its normal coordinates are nonzero. No target plane,
primitive vector, rank premise or host count is postulated.

All these finite results are unconditional. The remaining
T1.16 obligation is the uniform tuple count
N^epsilon*(N^3/T^2+N^(6/5)), including actual CRT encoding,
hyperbolic reciprocal sums and the fixed-k induction. No new
external input is added. Coverage stays 79/167; main 3.3 stays
conditional and T1.12 clauses (2),(3) remain open. Confirmed
mathematical improvements total 114, with the exact finite
scope of the new finding retained. Original source bytes,
compiler and dependency pins are unchanged; no new Paper C
source is copied and Palomar remains deferred.

## Actual ternary groups: both CRT counting regimes

The two CRT counting regimes in the proof of companion T1.16
are now proved on actual finite center populations, with the
three sets of values, their prime cutoff and their height cap
allowed to vary after the uniform threshold and with the center.
The sets themselves are never enumerated. The finite covers
enumerate only actual group products, their ordered positive
factorizations and bounded integer offsets.

IntegerOffsetCRT cancels arbitrary signed integer offsets in
two divisibility conditions and proves equality of the residue
classes. Pairwise coprimality combines all moduli. Each actual
coordinate in an interval of length N has at most N/Q+1 values;
an actual d-dimensional population has at most (N/Q+1)^d points.
No CRT solution is chosen, and no lower endpoint or offset
positivity is required. PlaneOffsetCRT proves that two actual
coordinates determine the third on an integer plane with
nonzero third normal coordinate. The corresponding count is
(N/Q+1)^2. The forced planes previously constructed have every
normal coordinate nonzero, so this condition is discharged.

ProductFactorizations constructs the actual finite pool of
ordered k-factor decompositions of Q, with cardinality at most
tau(Q)^k. The already proved elementary divisor estimate yields
a uniform subpower bound at every fixed polynomial product
height. CRTProductCover constructs the actual center cover,
including its coprimality and divisibility filters. Its offset
pool has exactly (2R+1)^(dk) members.

FiniteCRTTails transfers finite positive integer and positive
pair sums into the already proved summable p-series and
hyperbolic tails. The elementary inequalities
(a+1)^3<=4(a^3+1), a>=0, and (a+1)^2<=2(a^2+1)
remove all intermediate reciprocal terms. The finite cubic
sum is at most 8N^3*T^(-2)+4V for T<q<=V. The finite square
sum over positive pairs with ab>T is at most
2*C_2*N^2*T^(-1)*log(2T)+2*#pairs. Thus the source's separate
reciprocal-product logarithmic-square sum is unnecessary.
This checked proof simplification is P1-MATH-0115.

CRTProductRange proves the weak-regime count, retaining the
literal offset factor and uniformly paying for actual ordered
factorizations by M^epsilon. PlaneProductCover proves the
strong-regime count over any actual finite plane pool and only
two positive group sizes. The positive-product divisor count
pays for the latter size pool by V*M^epsilon. The third group
is not enumerated a second time.

TernaryTopProducts defines the actual maximum over products of
k distinct active groups, with value zero when too few exist.
The maximum is proved attained whenever positive, and every
selected product is bounded by it. Injective finite enumerations
give its actual group vectors. TernaryGroupCertificates proves
that these groups supply the actual offset-CRT certificates.
For a triple with product above 6AH^2 and whose squared product
exceeds T^3, an actual pair has product>T and <=2A(H+1), and the
center belongs to the actual two-group cover of the previously
constructed finite plane pool. No count or plane is postulated.

TernaryGroupCounts proves both uniform regimes for arbitrary
finite center populations with center-dependent arithmetic
sets. The weak bound is
M^epsilon*(2R+1)^(3k)*(8N^3/T^2+4V).
The strong bound is the exact plane-pool cardinality times
(2R+1)^6 times
(2*C_2*N^2*log(2T)/T+2V*M^epsilon).
All local data injectivity, disjointness, positive value and
diameter hypotheses in the strong bound are the actual
arithmetic predicates. The top-product height bound <=A^k is
also proved from actual group divisibility. These statements
have no new external input and no assumed target count.

The final critical-band absorption, the choice V=N^(6/5), and
the fixed-k induction remain open. Accordingly T1.16 stays
in_progress, numbered coverage stays 79/167, and main 3.3 stays
conditional. Confirmed improvements total 115. The compiler,
dependency pins and original manuscript bytes are unchanged;
no new Paper C source is copied and Palomar remains deferred.

## Companion T1.16: the full actual ternary group budget

Companion Proposition T1.16 is now proved unconditionally,
including its actual tuple count, the final critical-band
absorption, the fixed-k induction, offset-pattern multiplicity,
and the source prime cutoff without an upper bound.
The public theorem is TernaryUnboundedCutoff.companion_T1_16;
actual_tuples_bound applies it to the literally defined finite
tuple population, not an abstract supplied count. The final
bound is N^epsilon*(N^3/T^2+N^(6/5)), for every fixed k>=3,
and in fact for every real T>=1, covering the printed range
1<=T<=N. The original common convention B=L+1 and critical
band is recorded in companion_sections/guide.tex:19-38.

One threshold, depending only on C,D,k,J,epsilon, precedes all
lengths and radii, the arbitrary type of offset-pattern labels,
their actual finite pool of size at most B^J, all actual center
populations, all assignments of the three arithmetic sets,
their cutoff choices, base intervals and the real threshold T.
The parameter J permits polynomially many actual pattern labels;
this includes the source's fixed number of offset patterns.
No regular-set, probability or affine-compatibility premise is
used. Values are actual positive integers of height at most DN,
within R<=DB of the centers. Center boxes have side length DN;
no lower center bound is required. A fixed natural D can enlarge
any fixed source height and width comparison constants.

TernaryGroupScales proves the exact polynomial bounds for the
offset and plane pools and their uniform critical-band absorption.
It proves 6(DN)H^2<N^(6/5) and 2(DN)(H+1)<=N^2 uniformly when
H<=DB, and bounds log(2N^(4/5)) by a fixed multiple of B.
The plane-pool and two-group-offset factor is bounded by
17^3*49*(2R+1)^15. All constants and fixed polynomial degrees
are paid for by positive power margins; no asymptotic factor
is inserted as an assumption.

TernaryWeakCritical proves the full weak count for any fixed k
and all T>=1, with product cutoff V arbitrary and nonnegative.
The actual group height <=DN proves topProduct<=N^(2k)
eventually, discharging the ordered-factorization height cap.
TernaryStrongCritical proves the actual three-group tail above
N^(6/5) is at most N^(6/5+epsilon). Its two-group threshold is
N^(4/5). The first term is N^2*N^(-4/5)*log(2N^(4/5)); the
second counts actual pairs of sizes with product O(NB), using
the already proved divisor estimate with a fixed margin 1/10.
The actual forced plane and finite offset pool are retained
throughout. Combining the weak and strong populations proves
the full three-group budget.

TernaryTopProductDrop deletes a smallest element of an actual
maximizing k-selection and proves
G_k^(k-1)<=G_(k-1)^k. Thus G_k>N^(6/5) forces
G_(k-1)>N^(6(k-1)/(5k)). For every k>=4 this exponent is at
least 9/10. The same preceding-order cutoff N^(9/10) therefore
works at every induction step, and N^3/N^(18/10)=N^(6/5).
This removes the source's separate k=4, k=5 and k>=6 cases.
The strong induction is fully proved in TernaryGroupBudget;
it does not accept a previous-order target bound as an external
argument. This simplification is recorded as P1-MATH-0116.

TernaryLargestSelection identifies an actual maximizing
k-selection with the k strictly largest active groups: every
outside group is strictly smaller than every selected group.
The previously proved active-value injectivity removes ties.
The canonical maximum product is zero when fewer than k active
groups exist. This aligns the finite maximum with the source's
decreasing-order convention without assuming a sorted list.

TernaryPatternBudget counts actual labeled tuples and absorbs
their B^J pattern multiplicity, with the threshold before the
label type. The source full even-map injectivity is explicitly
converted to the weaker local parity injectivity used by the
internal budget. Pairwise disjoint actual even images are
retained. No local kernel or directness condition is hidden.

The source only requires H to exceed the three diameters;
there is no upper bound on H in the final public statement.
TernaryCutoffMonotonicity proves actual prime-pool inclusion,
group divisibility and size monotonicity, active-support
inclusion and top-product monotonicity. Replace H internally
by min(H,2R+1): this still dominates the actual diameters and
has a fixed logarithmic ceiling, while every counted top
product can only increase. TernaryUnboundedCutoff proves this
reduction and the final actual finite-tuple theorem. The
source cutoff may vary both with the pattern and the center.

T1.16 moves from in_progress to proved. Numbered coverage is

Main 3.3 and the other identified geometric applications stay

## T21.4: actual polylogarithmic group confinement in three dimensions

The full three-dimensional support-group branch of companion
T21.4 is now proved on actual finite tuple populations. The
individual-prime branch and the fixed-affine-plane variant
remain open, so the numbered proposition moves from not_started
to in_progress, not proved. Coverage stays 80/167 and confirmed
improvements stay 116; this is a proof-composition advance.

ProductConfinement proves the deterministic finite argument.
If all selected k-products of a finite factor set are <=N,
at most k-1 factors exceed N^(1/k). If the remaining product
exceeds N, a minimum-cardinality crossing subset has product
in (N,N^(1+1/k)] and all its factors are <=N^(1/k). Otherwise
the count of factors>Y is at most floor(log N/log Y), proved
by the actual finite logarithm-of-product identity. These
claims require neither primality nor an assumed stopping rule.

TernaryValueConfinement applies this to the actual group-value
pool. Group values and support labels have the same cardinality
by actual active-value injectivity. Their pairwise coprimality
is proved, every selected product is bounded by the actual top
product, and the crossing subset is shown to provide genuine
integer-offset CRT certificates for its actual centers.

CRTSupportCover canonically enumerates a finite set A of factor
sizes, rather than paying for all their orderings. The offset
cost is exactly (2R+1)^(3*card A). A certificate product Q>N
in a box of side DN has at most (D+1)^3 centers for each offset
assignment. The actual finite cover over all such A is bounded
by (D+1)^3 times the literal integer-factor weighted count of
T21.3. Coprimality is retained while applying CRT and only then
dropped in the positive Rankin sum. No target count is assumed.

RankinCertificateCritical combines that actual cover with the
already proved T21.3 integer-factor bound and the verified
sublinear-logarithmic exponential estimate. For any fixed
0<zeta<1 and k>=1 its count is at most
N^((1+1/k)*(1+(2+zeta)/c)+epsilon), uniformly over critical
lengths and bounded radii, all center base intervals and all
actual integer factor subsets. PolylogConfinementScales chooses
zeta and k before N so the extra exponent is arbitrarily small.
It also proves, uniformly in the critical band, that
k-1+floor(log N/(c log B))=o(L), with a literal statement for
every positive comparison constant and B=L+1.

TernaryGroupConfinement proves the actual exceptional-center
count N^(max(6/5,1+2/c)+epsilon). The first population has actual
topProduct>N and is counted by the completed T1.16. Every point
in the second population supplies an actual crossing certificate
and belongs to the Rankin cover. The two populations cover the
entire excessive-group family. The integer k depends only on
c,epsilon and precedes C,D, the actual sets and cutoff choices.
The source cutoff has no upper bound here.

LabeledPopulationCount proves a general finite label-fiber count.
TernaryConfinementMass uses it to include B^J actual offset-pattern
labels, with one threshold before the label type, all arithmetic
assignments and nonnegative weights. For point weights at most
N^(-beta+epsilon/2), the actual excessive-group population has
mass at most
N^(-min(beta-6/5,beta-1-2/c)+epsilon).
The remaining error margin pays for the count and labels. This
is the source's uniform N^(-beta+o(1)) weight regime made explicit;
it is not an assumed exceptional-count or exceptional-mass bound.
The actual exceptional finite set is defined, its mass is bounded,
and every retained tuple has at most
k-1+floor(log N/(c log B)) actual groups greater than B^c.

TernaryGroupNegligibility proves that c>6 makes
max(6/5,1+2/c)<4/3. It supplies a fixed positive point-weight
margin theta and a fixed k such that for every eta>0, eventually
the actual exceptional mass is <=eta*L*N^(-2/3), whenever each
host weight is in the beta=2 class, at most N^(-2+theta).
The retained count is the same literal source expression. This
is the sufficient c>6 assertion for the three-dimensional group
branch. No c>3 fixed-plane claim is made at this checkpoint.

The remaining T21.4 work is explicit: the individual-prime
fixed-k budget must account for repeated offset supports, and
the specified-plane CRT cover must enumerate only two free
offset coordinates to obtain the 1/c exponent and c>3 threshold.
No new literature input, Paper C copy, original source change,
dependency update or Palomar registration is introduced.

TernaryIndividualPrimes constructs the actual finite pool of

block. Its membership is the literal existence of a support

retains arbitrary source cutoffs with no upper bound by the

TernaryPrimeValueConfinement supplies the deterministic
confinement-or-certificate alternative for actual primes>B^c.

within the explicitly stated positive-host-weight regime; it

## Complete companion T21.4: polylogarithmic confinement

Companion Proposition T21.4 is now complete, including both
actual support groups and actual individual primes, all ordinary

and the sufficient c>6 and c>3 thresholds. It moves from

mathematical improvements stay 118. This checkpoint closes the
remaining source obligations without a new correction identifier.

FreePlaneCRT proves that only two congruence coordinates are
needed on any genuine real affine plane. Choose a coordinate
with nonzero normal entry and project onto its two complementary
coordinates. The finite sum identity isolates the omitted
coordinate, proving injectivity of this projection. The actual
integer-offset residue population therefore has at most
(width/Q+1)^2 points. Plane coefficients are arbitrary real
numbers: there is no rationality, height or quantitative lower
bound on the nonzero normal coefficient. One common threshold
precedes the actual choice of planes and coefficients.

PlaneSupportCover defines actual finite plane-restricted CRT
populations. The canonical enumeration of a factor set A costs
exactly (2R+1)^(2*card A) offset codes. The third offset is never
an enumeration label. All three possible omitted coordinates
are covered by a factor 3. For Q>N and width DN, summing over
the actual finite plane pool gives the finite bound
3*#planes*(D+1)^2*integerWeightedCount(Y,V,(2R+1)^2).
Actual three-coordinate certificates restricted to a genuine
plane are proved to belong to this new two-coordinate cover.
This transfers both previously constructed group and prime
crossing certificates without assuming a plane-count estimate.

PlaneRankinCritical applies the already proved integer-factor
Rankin bound with d=2. With at most B^K actual planes, its
critical-band certificate count is at most
N^((1+1/k)*(1+(1+zeta)/c)+epsilon).
The arbitrary plane family, all coefficients, center intervals,
lengths, offsets and factor sets vary after the common threshold.
The polynomial plane multiplicity and the sublinear-logarithmic
exponential are absorbed using proved estimates. There is no
new external geometric or analytic argument.

PlaneTernaryConfinement proves a single simultaneous exceptional
count for excessive support-group OR individual-prime populations.
The two actual top-product>N populations are bounded by the
completed fixed-k budgets. In the remaining population, either
excess supplies an actual crossing certificate; its genuine
plane places the point in the two-coordinate Rankin cover.
The resulting count is N^(max(6/5,1+1/c)+epsilon).
The same parameter choice k,zeta already used in three dimensions
suffices, because the d=2 excess exponent is smaller.

PlaneConfinementMass includes B^J actual offset-pattern labels
and up to B^K real planes for each label. A common threshold
precedes the label type, all actual assignments and all weights.
Its actual_plane_confinement theorem defines the actual common
exceptional finite set and proves its positive mass at most
N^(-min(beta-6/5,beta-1-1/c)+epsilon).
Outside it, BOTH the actual support-group and individual-prime
counts above B^c are bounded by the same
k-1+floor(log N/(c log B)). The source point-weight regime is
made explicit as 0<=w<=N^(-beta+epsilon/2). Uniform o(1) point
errors fit this regime eventually; neither an exceptional count

PolylogConfinementTheorem.companion_T21_4_three_dimensional
likewise provides ONE actual exceptional set and a common k for

of an arbitrary nonnegative local Euler product over a finite
set of distinct primes. For every natural X, the average over

MaximalSupportWord proves an elementary finite coding fact:
some binary codeword has weight at least the code dimension.
Choose a word of maximal support; restriction of the code to
that support is injective, since a nonzero kernel word has
disjoint support and increases the chosen support after
addition. The dimension is bounded by that restriction's
target dimension. For an even code and even t, dimension
at least t-1 therefore yields a word of weight at least t.
No pivot coordinates or simultaneous block support are
assumed or supplied as external data.

PrimitiveCoordinateProjection proves every coordinate
projection of a minimal effective relation kernel is
INJECTIVE. A kernel vector vanishing at that coordinate
restricts to the proper erased family; its nullity zero
forces the restriction to vanish, and extension by zero
recovers the whole vector. Hence every projection image has
dimension equal to the entire primitive nullity.
HeavyPhysicalRelations uses the previously proved
effective_projection_rank_le and the actual surjection
from physical even relations to effective relations.
The coding lemma then constructs an ACTUAL global physical
even relation with at least t selected values at any
prescribed block. PrimitiveAnchorWitnesses consequently
gives the literal15.11 witness predicate whenever
rho>=t-1. Different blocks may use different relations.
In particular every primitive has two-anchor witnesses,

The strict cutoff and graph gaps are verified by exact

## Whole compressed-pair mass at all cardinalities

The WHOLE, unseparated clause of companion T15.1 is now proved at its

parameters are selected before their explicit geometric hypotheses, then
one threshold is selected before N,L, every actual dyadic subground G and
EVERY subpopulation of actual primitive compressed extensions. The sum is

  sum_(e,A) u^(|A|+2) [ q(e union A) + |compressed_c(e,A)| + |c(e union A)| ]
       <= N^(-1+epsilon).

The source pair remains distinguished in this sum. All cardinalities,
nonempty targets, heterogeneous actual marginals, affine incompatibility
and zero marginals are retained. The new finite theorem proves the
coefficient really is the expectation of the centered source INDICATOR
as one block times the centered individual target indicators. Its exact

configurations. It is not a homogeneous rank weight treated as a joint
probability or a product of separately centered source endpoints.

PrimitiveCompressionCriterion.primitive_iff proves the exact equivalence

RelationLossMonotonicity proves actual deletion-loss monotonicity by zero

at most L. Canonical connectedness of the original union is proved: both
source endpoints must lie in one canonical block because their intersection

subfamily of the internally direct target set.

The original union has the following exhaustive rank dichotomy. If either
source or compressed nullity is at most2, total actual nullity is at most
L+2. Otherwise every original coordinate has deletion loss at least3, so
the union is an actual4-core with total actual nullity at most2L.

## Exact original once/all coupling and optimal Wasserstein cost

Stable ID: P1-PROB-ONCE-ALL-ORIGINAL-COUPLING. Status: proved, unconditional exact finite original TV/transport inequalities and optimality; coarse rate-one and first-order negligibility conditional on the existing finite coarse connected bundle. T19.10 and T1.17 retain their sharp numerical obligations.

The finite probabilistic coupling assertions of companion T19.10 are now
proved for the ACTUAL ORIGINAL once-erased and good-isolated count laws:
0 <= beta-r <= E[(Xi)_2]/2, TV <= E[(Xi)_2]/2 and W1 <= E[(Xi)_2].
No arithmetic estimate for the target second moment is a premise of
these exact finite inequalities. T19.10 remains IN PROGRESS only for
its numerical O(a_N^2) conclusions, which still require the sharper
positive two-good-edge upper bound of T1.17. Numbered coverage remains
87/167 unconditional and46 conditional.

FirstWasserstein defines the usual discrete transport infimum on N.
A plan is a nonnegative matrix with the prescribed probability rows
and columns, and summable cost mass(i,j)*|i-j|. The matrix has summable
total mass exactly one. The real-valued infimum explicitly requires
the existence of a finite-cost plan; it is never used on an empty
cost set. Its nonnegativity and comparison with every plan are proved.
For ANY pair of finite observations of the same sample, finitePlan
is their literal joint mass matrix. Its row and column marginal
identities and exact expected absolute cost are proved.

FirstWassersteinTests proves absolute summability and exact marginal
identities for ANY integrable real test under EVERY transport plan.
Every one-Lipschitz test gives a lower bound for the transport cost
and for the infimum. The attained total-variation test is one-Lipschitz
on N, giving TV <= W1 with the probability convention for TV.
FirstWassersteinFinite applies the identity test to prove that ANY
finite ordered coupling W<=Z is optimal, with W1=E[Z]-E[W]. These
lower bounds are proved for all competing transport plans; no
optimality or distance comparison is assumed.

FiniteOnceAllCoupling proves the pointwise natural-count inequalities
with the exact constants: the disagreement indicator is at most
(k)_2/2 and the absolute count cost is at most (k)_2, for the actual
active-edge count k. The two deterministic observations share the
same finite binary field and the same arbitrary finite probability.
Their actual TV and transport bounds follow without independence.

OnceAllOriginalCoupling constructs the actual original sample plan.
Its factorialCost_eq_second identifies the finite expectation with
the infinite prime-sign second factorial moment; factorialSecond_eq_joint
identifies that moment with the ordered distinct-edge union joint sum.
good_bounds has all three literal T19.10 inequalities with constants
one half, one half and one. The once law is the genuine previously
constructed uniform-deletion count law, identified EXACTLY with the
deterministic observation Z-2*1_(some good edge active); the other law
is the genuine original all-good-edge isolation law.

OnceAllMeanCost proves, UNCONDITIONALLY for every H,N,L, the sharper
identity W1=actual once mean-actual isolated mean. Thus the natural
coupling is optimal. It also proves the order of the actual means
and TV <= their difference. This is improvement P1-MATH-0159 and can
be added to the future statement or proof of T19.10.

OnceAllCouplingUnderInputs uses only the EXISTING coarse connected
geometry to prove BOTH E[(Xi)_2] <= N^(-1+epsilon) and the SUM of
the activation correction, TV and W1 <= N^(-1+epsilon), uniformly
over ALL real H in the critical band. Parameters4 are chosen first

## Asymmetric profile: a necessary alignment-scope correction

Stable ID: P1-DIOPH-ASYMMETRIC-ALIGNMENT-SCOPE. Status: unconditional obstruction to the literal radius-one statement; the proposed enlarged-radius profile is unproved. No external result is an input.

Companion T1.10 has a confirmed ALIGNMENT-SCOPE CORRECTION,
P1-MATH-0162. Its printed assertion cannot hold with the main article's
literal definition of nonalignment, namely reduced positive slopes up
to B^3 and displacement at most (r+s)*B. The old set is allowed a wider
interval X+[-D*B,D*B], but the exclusion has not been enlarged with it.
This is a source-statement correction, separate from the 161 improvements.
Numbered coverage remains87/167 unconditional and48 conditional. T1.10
is in progress; neither its printed estimate nor a corrected replacement
is marked proved or used as a new input.

The unconditional checked family has L=3k, B=3k+1, X=2t,
z=3t+3B and U_X=[X,X+3B] (so the permitted old-width constant is D=3).
For j=0,...,k-1, target index3j+1 has actual value3(t+B+j), while
the old set contains2(t+B+j). Above EVERY cutoff H>=3 these two values
have identical parity vectors. Their zero-sum selections give
delta*(X,z)>=k-1. The loss is the literal preimage dimension of the
new even-selection map under the old RAW value span after forgetting
small-prime coordinates; no old parity or selected-map injectivity
is silently imposed. EvenPreimageRank proves the general injection
underlying this dimension lower bound.

For t>5B^4 these pairs are nonaligned at the ORIGINAL radius,
uniformly over ALL reduced slopes up to B^3. The determinant estimate
forces any possible slope to be2:3, whose displacement is6B>5B.
The same pairs ARE aligned at radius2. Thus the radius enlargement
suggested below actually excludes this entire obstruction. The new
window is separated from the source by more than L.

For m=2^(3k), N=6m and 3m<=t<4m-B, both centres lie in [N,2N).
There are exactly m-B distinct pairs. The full actual nonaligned
profile for the deterministic rule U_X=[X,X+3B] is at least
(m-B)*(2^(k-1)-1), and for all sufficiently large k it is at least
m^(4/3)/8. The sequence lies in the literal critical band with C=3.
At epsilon=1/48 the printed exponent is31/24+1/48=21/16<4/3.
AsymmetricAlignmentScopeObstruction.no_uniform_radius_one_bound
therefore rules out ANY uniform constant and threshold, for EVERY
fixed positive integer multiple H=q*(L+1), including arbitrarily large
fixed multiples. Its profile definition sums (2^delta*-1) over the
literal dyadic radius-one nonaligned population, with the actual old
interval and even-selection loss. The obstruction does not depend on
any external geometry, Reuss estimate, probabilistic input or conjecture.

Suggested revision: explicitly define asymmetric nonalignment with an
exclusion radius depending on D, for example max(1,D)*(r+s)*B, or the
corresponding sharper bound from the two unequal offset widths. Reprove
T1.10 with that exclusion and check how the enlarged aligned sector is
handled wherever T1.10 is used. The present result proves that a change
is NECESSARY and that radius2 already removes this test family; it does
NOT prove that this change alone suffices for the asserted31/24 bound
or all downstream estimates. No main-article conclusion is refuted by
this counterexample. The original manuscripts remain byte-for-byte
unchanged. Palomar remains a later milestone.

## Specified private signed forcing and its finite directed cost

Stable ID: P1-ARITH-PRIVATE-SIGNED-FORCING-FINITE. Full construction and finite identities proved internally; precisely pinned Apache-2.0 PaperC fragments recompiled. No reciprocal-pivot asymptotic, PNT or cost bound is assumed. T19.16 remains in progress.

The SPECIFIED signed private-pivot forcing of companionT19.16 is now
constructed in the actual finite P1 prime-sign cylinder, including the
full signed field and its nonnegative coordinate cost. This is preparatory
progress: the exact logarithmic cost equivalent is NOT proved, andT19.16
is IN PROGRESS. Coverage remains88/167 unconditional and69 conditional;
10 numbered results remain incomplete. T19.15's precise reciprocal-pivot
asymptotic andT19.17's universal anchor obstruction remain separate.

PrivateValueSystem and PrivatePivotGeometry prove that the largest prime
with odd valuation gives the actual prime basis of every retained raw
word. A pivot at least the word length is private by modular cancellation.
Its own parity is exactly1, and all off-diagonal valuations vanish.
The prime2 is included; the valuation is not required to equal1. No upper
quadratic size restriction is introduced. Every pivot belongs to the
same actual finite prime cylinder as its positive integer argument.

PrivateCoordinateForcing works above ANY finite normalized background law,
including one already conditioned. PrivatePrimeForcing constructs the
actual deterministic correction of the selected prime signs. It fixes all
nonpivots, fixes already satisfied samples and is idempotent. It hits the
prescribed word. Uniform translation and finite Fubini prove the complete
conditional-law identity for EVERY observable of the entire prime sample;
the law of the displayed word alone is not substituted for this assertion.

PrivateHardConditionalForcing proves that the entire actual small-prime
trace is unchanged. The exact conditional identity holds for any real
weight of that trace, including soft tilts, and any event of it. When the
event has positive probability, positivity of the marked event is proved
as part of the full conditional-law assertion. No assumed Palm law enters
the actual construction.

SignedExactWords identifies the event with the existing P1 StartEvent,
an exact right boundary and the actual sign. The bit word is proved to
be the literal signed multiplicative word(-sigma,sigma,...,sigma,-sigma).
The left word boundaryj is the source run startj+1. SignedPrivatePalmForcing
prescribes ONLY the actualL+e+2 values; the maximalL+E+2 support certifies
the pivot hypotheses but adds no forced equations. The exact marginal
is2^(-L-e-2)=p*2^(-e-2). Both signs and every0<=e<=E are retained. Their
total mass at a source is exactlyp*(1-2^(-E-1))<=p, so no spurious factor
growing withE is paid in the type sum.

SignedPrivateField constructs this complete finite field, its actual
forcing maps, its weighted full-observable Palm identity and its directed
affected set. All target raw values, hence the entire exact marked target,
are unchanged outside that set. SignedPrivateDyadicField identifies the
literal dyadic starts retained by the manuscript: every maximal-support
pivot exceedsY=2*(L+E+2). Subtracting1 gives exactly their left boundaries,
with an explicitly proved inverse and cardinality at mostN. The field
contains both signs and all excesses at every retained start. Its total
actual mean is at mostN*p for every finite cutoffE.

ForcingCoordinateCost uses the literal sum of absolute coordinate
differences between the original field and the forced field after
deleting its source. The exact decomposition is

  cost = sum_a lambda_a^2 + sum_a lambda_a*expected_offsite_cost_a.

The diagonal is retained, not absorbed into an assumed conditional error.
For any directed footprint containing every affected target, the finite
upper ledger is

  cost <= sum_a lambda_a^2
          + sum_a sum_{b!=a in footprint_a}(lambda_a*lambda_b+P(W_a=W_b=1)).

The generic lemma lists its Palm identity explicitly; SignedPrivateField
DISCHARGES it from the actual prime forcing and proves the required
pointwise preservation. Thus this is an actual field estimate, not an
implication assuming the intended coupling law or cost bound. The source
is removed only in the offsite sum. It is a positive coordinate cost,
not a claimed lower bound for total variation or a signed scalar residual.

PrivateDirectedFootprint proves the actual arithmetic ledger in every
translated interval. For source word lengthB, target diameterQ, interval
lengthN and source left-boundary setJ whose values lie in[1,X],

  sum_{j inJ} |directed_footprint_j|
    <= (Q+1)*(N*B*S_kappa(X)+|J|*B).

All floors are literal. The proof counts multiples in translated intervals,
sums the actual reciprocal pivots and uses the injective shiftj->j+i for
each source position. It neither assumes a dependency graph nor counts
selected pivot witnesses as distinct source words. The finite inequality
precedes every reciprocal-pivot asymptotic.

Seven precisely pinned PaperC sources supply selected raw-value, pivot,
forcing and signed-word arguments. Their Git blob hashes were recomputed
from the fetched bytes and agree exactly with the immutable source tree.
Apache-2.0 attribution and statement comparisons are retained in headers
andPAPER_C_REUSE.md. The old Lean4.34 compiled artifacts, probability PMF
interfaces, analytic saddle/PNT inputs and unrelated marked-process
dependencies are not imported. Every selected fragment is rebuilt under
Lean v4.36.0-rc2 using the existing P1 probability and arithmetic model.

P1-MATH-0179 records the stronger finite conditional/soft-weight identity,

## Arbitrary arithmetic anchors and exact finite flip costs

Stable ID: P1-ARITH-ANCHORED-FORCING-FINITE-FLIPS. All actual anchored conditional maps, original event identifications and independent finite word flip laws are proved internally. No smooth-value density, arithmetic pair count or target cost exponent is an input. T19.16 andT19.17 remain in progress.

CompanionT19.17 now has an actual finite construction for EVERY
admissible arithmetic anchor, together with both literal unsigned word
events and their complete conditional laws. Its asymptotic universal
anchor obstruction is NOT proved:T19.17 is IN PROGRESS. CompanionT19.16
also gains its exact finite signed single-flip mechanism. Both numbered
results remain incomplete. Coverage remains88/167 unconditional and69
conditional;10 numbered results remain open.

AnchoredPrivateValues proves that raw multiplicative values at products
v_i*v_anchor encode precisely the differences of the original raw bits.
Thus prescribing these relative rows is exactly prescribing the actual
original word up to one global sign. The products are only an exact
algebraic encoding; no product pivot or extra prime sign is introduced.
All displayed integer arguments are positive and multiplicativity is
proved in the same original prime cylinder.

AnchoredWindowPivots constructs the actual largest odd-valuation pivot
at every NONANCHOR vertex. Only those pivots must exceed the word
diameter. Their basis property holds for the relative raw-value system;
they are distinct and none divides the original anchor argument. The
anchor itself can have a small pivot or even be a square. Its raw value
need not be fair, nonconstant or private.

AnchoredPrivateForcing prescribes the relative rows by modifying only
these nonanchor primes. It preserves the anchor value, fixes every
already admissible word, and is idempotent. The actual output orientation
is determined by the ORIGINAL anchor bit and the chosen template. It
proves the complete conditional sample law for all full observables,
and the weighted identity for arbitrary real functions of the small-prime
trace. The whole small-prime environment remains unchanged. No independent
or uniformly distributed anchor bit is assumed for this conditional law.

AnchoredWindowForcing proves that the rule "every small pivot in the
actual word must be the anchor" is EXACTLY the required nonanchor privacy
condition. An actual anchor exists when at most one actual-word pivot
is small. The count of small vertices is monotone under enlarging the
word, so the manuscript's maximal-support retention supplies existence
for each shorter actual word. The anchor parameter is arbitrary and
chosen before the random sample; no particular selection algorithm or
factorization tie-breaking rule is imposed.

UnsignedAnchoredRunForcing identifies BOTH source events exactly:
theL+1 word is the original StartEvent, and theL+2 word is exact excess
zero with either sign. For every admissible anchor their actual means
are respectively2^(-L)=p and2^(-L-1)=p/2. Their forcing laws are the
full conditional prime-assignment laws, not just marginal word identities.
These statements include a defective or deterministic anchor. Positivity
and the number of independent relative equations are proved, rather than
supplied as a Palm or rank premise.

BinaryForcingFlip proves the finite lower mechanism for arbitrary
source orientations. For two original bitsX,Y and any chosen orientationxi,
the number of changed candidate bits dominates the indicator of
X+Y+b+c=1. Consequently, if this ORIGINAL parity is fair, the two flip
probabilities sum to at least1/2 and one is at least1/4. Fairness ofxi is
NOT required for this local balance. The fair original parity is proved
internally for distinct coordinates of a uniform raw word, by an actual
single-coordinate translation of its finite uniform law. The same method
proves that the prescribed signed flip, and a nonanchor flip in the
deterministic anchored forcing, are fair on that uniform source word.

WordForcingFlipCost constructs an independent uniform target by a nested
finite average. A specified signed word and its single-coordinate
translate are disjoint. An unsigned two-orientation word orbit and its
single-coordinate translate are also disjoint when the word has at least
two positions. Their actual masses are exactly2^(-B) and2^(-(B-1)).
For a source flip of probabilityr, the expected absolute target change
is EXACTLY2*r times the target mass. A fair flip therefore costs exactly
one target mass; a flip probability at least1/4 costs at least half a
target mass. The actual signed source correction and actual deterministic
anchor correction are instantiated on the uniform source word.

The two-candidate half-mass lower mechanism is also instantiated for an
ARBITRARY functionxi of the uniform source word, without assuming its
marginal fairness. This finite strengthening concerns the positive
coordinate cost. Fairness may still be relevant to whether a chosen
random orientation realizes a particular full Palm law. No unconditional
Palm claim is made for an arbitrary orientation rule.

The finite flip lemmas explicitly realize source/target independence;
they do NOT assert that all actual arithmetic pairs are independent.
The clean arithmetic pair selection, quantitative collision/valuation
exclusions, ordinary smooth-value short-interval theorem, reciprocal-pivot
asymptotic and final asymptotic lower sums remain open. In particular the
fullT19.17 factor1/2 andT19.16 logarithmic equivalent are not counted as
completed merely from these local mechanisms.

P1-MATH-0180 records the arbitrary-anchor conditional law without a
fair-anchor assumption and the stronger fairness-free LOCAL orientation
balance. There are179 confirmed improvements and one statement-scope
correction. All proofs are new P1 code above the previously attributed
private-forcing foundation. No new PaperC port, analytic input, axiom,
compiler/dependency change or original manuscript edit is introduced.
Palomar remains deferred until full coverage and statement alignment.

## Clean directed arithmetic pairs and actual target cost

Stable ID: P1-ARITH-CLEAN-PIVOT-ACTUAL-COST-LEDGER. Finite arithmetic counts and prime-cylinder cost identities proved internally. The joint raw matrix must be surjective; its failure-set cardinality and the analytic asymptotics are not assumed. T19.16/T19.17 remain in progress.

Companion T19.16 and T19.17 gain a finite clean arithmetic pair
ledger and exact positive target costs in the ORIGINAL prime cylinder.
Both numbered results remain IN PROGRESS: no asymptotic forcing lower
bound, logarithmic equivalent or ordinary smooth-value theorem is assumed
or claimed. Coverage stays 88/167 unconditional and 69 conditional, with
10 numbered results incomplete.

CleanPivotMultiples proves both sides of the actual multiple count in
every translated positive interval (A,A+N], with literal natural floors:

  floor(N/q) <= number of q-multiples <= floor(N/q)+1,
  N/q-1 <= number of q-multiples <= N/q+1.

For coprime q,r, the count satisfying q|n and r|n+k is at most
floor(N/(q*r))+1, uniformly in the interval position and offset k.
The proof uses differences from the least actual solution. It does not
postulate the existence or density of a CRT residue class.

CleanPivotTargets retains q|n, excludes q^2|n and excludes every other
selected prime r from every target position 0..B-1. The membership test
and the finite union/deletion ledger are exact. If q>=Y>0 and every r>=Y,
with each r coprime to q, its actual clean target count is at least

  N/q - 1 - (|R|*B+1)*(N/(q*Y)+1).

This separates the valuation loss from every other-pivot collision and
keeps all endpoint +1 terms. No scale restriction on Y or B is used.

CleanPivotPairs retains each distinguished source j and sums its actual
target fibre injectively. Put S_q=sum_{j in J}1/q_j and suppose each
source has at most S other selected primes. The total clean directed
pair count is at least

  N*S_q - |J| - (S*B+1)*((N/Y)*S_q+|J|).

After deleting arbitrary exceptional target set T and arbitrary exceptional
PAIR set D, the same lower bound loses only |J|*|T|+|D|. In particular a
global exceptional pair set is charged ONCE, rather than once per source.
Neither set's cardinality is assumed small. All finite counts precede
the reciprocal-pivot, smooth-value and raw-dependence asymptotics.

PrivatePivotTargetFlip connects those literal divisibility predicates
to the actual arithmetic field. The original forceWord changes a raw
value by the sum of its true selected-prime parity contributions. If q is prime,
q divides n and q^2 does not divide n, its valuation at n is exactly
ONE and hence its parity is one. Privacy above the
target width excludes that prime from the other target positions. Every
other changed prime is excluded by the actual clean-target predicate.
Thus the entire original target vector changes by exactly

  targetWord_after = targetWord_before + single_0(source_correction).

For the anchored map the correction is the exact original source bit
minus its template bit and anchor-determined orientation. No arbitrary
target flip is substituted for this physical prime modification. The
other-prime population has at most card(source)-1 elements. Its coprimeness
and cutoff conditions follow from actual distinct prime coordinates.

UniformLinearObservation proves that a surjective finite binary linear
map has the full uniform output law for every real observable, using the
existing actual affine fibre probabilities. RawWordObservation applies
this to the JOINT original source and target raw-value matrix. Its
surjectivity gives the actual independent uniform two-word law.
Clean divisibility alone does NOT imply this surjectivity. That finite
matrix condition remains explicit in each pointwise expected-cost theorem.

CleanPivotWordCost combines the actual target transformation with that
proved observation law. For a clean target with a surjective joint matrix,
the expected absolute change of a prescribed signed target word of length
B is EXACTLY 2^(-B). For a deterministic anchored source and an unsigned
two-orientation target of length B>=2, it is EXACTLY 2^(-(B-1)). These
are expectations in the original finite prime cylinder. Source/target
independence is discharged from matrix surjectivity; no conditional Palm
law or cost value is a theorem premise. The finite correction rates match
the signed and anchored uniform-word calculations already proved.

PositiveForcingCostLower identifies the full directed offsite sum with
the original nonnegative coordinate-cost ledger. Every selected clean
directed pair can be retained for a lower bound. The diagonal remains
separate and nonnegative, so the same selected-pair lower bound applies
to the full source-deleted cost. There is no cancellation, unordered-pair
quotient or implicit symmetry factor.

The final dyadic population restoration, quantitative bounds for the
exceptional target and raw-dependence pair sets, the ordinary smooth-value
short-interval input, sharp reciprocal-pivot saddle comparison and final
asymptotic summations remain unformalized. The finite arithmetic counts
and actual pointwise expected costs are not counted as a completed
T19.16 or T19.17. The existing half-count theorem uses EVEN effective
selections and is not silently applied to full raw-value relations.

P1-MATH-0181 records the explicit clean arithmetic deletion constants,
the once-only global pair-exception charge, and the actual prime-cylinder
single-bit cost bridge. There are 180 confirmed improvements and one
statement-scope correction. All new arguments use existing P1/Mathlib
foundations, with no new PaperC port, external mathematical premise,
dependency download, compiler change, axiom or source-manuscript edit.
Palomar remains deferred until full coverage and statement alignment.

## Unrestricted raw-dependence hosts in logarithmic windows

Stable ID: P1-RAW-DEPENDENCE-UNRESTRICTED-LOG-HOSTS. Unrestricted raw host count and actual joint-matrix failure count proved internally, without parity restrictions or external arithmetic premises. T19.16/T19.17 remain in progress.

Companion T19.16 and T19.17 now have the unconditional uniform full
RAW two-window dependence exception bound. For every fixed D>=0 and
epsilon>0 there is a threshold N0, independent of the moving width,
word lengths and prime-cylinder cutoff, such that for N>=N0,
1<=B<=D*log N, S,T<=B and M>=2N+B,

  # {(x,y) in [N,2N)^2 : the joint S/T raw-word matrix is not surjective}
       <= N^(3/2+epsilon).

The words are the actual original values x-1+i and y-1+j. No evenness
condition is imposed on either block. Local relations, repeated windows,
and diagonal host pairs are included. This fills the full raw host
exception estimate used in the lower-bound arguments; it does not prove
the final forcing asymptotics or mark either numbered result complete.

RawTwoWindowHosts defines the full nonzero two-block parity relation.
At least one selected coordinate anchors the relation, in one of the two
orientations. Every actual largeOddKernel is at least one, so the cutoff
T=1/2 retains every such anchor. Applying the existing unconditional
LargeAnchorPairs finite bound with tau=1/2 yields

  #hosts <= 8*B*N*sqrt(3N)*exp(K*sqrt B),
  K=2+PowerSeriesTail.constant(3/2).

In particular the argument requires neither prime number theory nor a
new PaperC port. It does not use the effective EVEN-space half-count.
UniformSubpolynomialPower converts the exact reciprocal-power convention
into a literal N^epsilon bound. RawTwoWindowHostCount proves that
8*sqrt(3)*(B+1)*exp(K*sqrt B) is uniformly subpolynomial throughout the
entire upper logarithmic band. The width need not have a fixed offset
from a critical length. The threshold is selected before the width.

RawValueIndependence proves the needed original matrix bridge. Injective
row relations give strictly positive mass to every output, hence
surjectivity. A non-surjective actual value system therefore supplies a
nonzero row relation. Evaluating it on every actual prime basis vector
recovers the full integer factorization-parity relation: primes above
the cutoff do not divide any positive observed integer, and nonprime
coordinates vanish. The two-block coefficient word splits into the two
unrestricted source and target selections. Thus non-surjectivity of the
joint raw matrix really is contained in the full arithmetic host set.
There is no independent-word premise in this exception count.

RawDependencePairs also proves that surjectivity for two maximal words
implies surjectivity for their shorter, possibly different, initial
segments, by extending both prescribed output words to the maximal
length. Rectangular non-surjectivity exceptions are therefore contained
in the same maximal bad-pair set. RawDependenceCount gives both literal
uniform bounds, with the cylinder cutoff quantified last and uniformly.

P1-MATH-0182 records this parity-complete raw exception estimate and its
actual finite-cylinder interpretation. The finite clean arithmetic
ledger can now discard raw-dependent pairs using a proved bound.
Endpoint translations, excluded-source/target counts, reciprocal-pivot
saddle comparison, full-value weighted upper profiles, ordinary smooth
integers in almost every short interval and final asymptotic cost
summations still require their own arguments. Neither T19.16 nor T19.17
is declared complete. Coverage remains 88 unconditional and 69
conditional results out of 167, with ten numbered results incomplete.
No source-manuscript byte, dependency or compiler version is changed.
Palomar remains deferred until completion and statement alignment.

## Polylogarithmic pivot exclusions and the actual clean-pair ledger

Stable ID: P1-POLYLOG-PIVOT-EXCEPTION-LEDGER. Actual small-pivot Rankin count and uniform clean-pair deletion ledger proved internally; ordinary smooth short-interval input and sharp reciprocal source asymptotics remain open. T19.16/T19.17 remain in progress.

Companion T19.16 and T19.17 gain proved polylogarithmic pivot
exception counts and a uniform clean-pair minorant with both actual
exceptional-set bounds discharged. Both results remain in progress.

PolylogPivotExceptions uses the actual largest prime with odd valuation,
including the prime two and the square convention kappa=1. The condition
kappa(n)<=Y is equivalent, for Y>=1, to truncated odd-prime kernel one.
The proved finite Rankin estimate gives, for 1/2<=sigma<1,

  # {1<=n<=X : kappa(n)<=Y}
  <= X^sigma/(1-sigma)*exp(Y^(1-sigma)/(1-sigma)).

Every bad start contains an actual bad value at a specified position.
The position fibre injects into the integer population, so a width B
window has at most B times that count. Its retained complement and exact
population-deletion identity are proved as finite-set statements.

For Y<=log(N)^5 choose sigma=9/10. The logarithmic identity
(log(N)^5)^(1/10)=sqrt(log N) converts the Euler factor into
exp(10*sqrt(log N)). PolylogPivotCount proves the actual value count
and, uniformly for every moving B<=D*log N, the bad-window count
N^(9/10+epsilon). All thresholds precede the width and cutoff. This
uses the existing internal Rankin bound and subpolynomial tools, not an
ordinary smooth-value theorem in almost every short interval.

ForcingExceptionalSets records the exact arithmetic translation.
For N>=2 the left boundaries of [N,2N) are precisely
(N-2,N-2+N], an interval of N positive integers. The arbitrary translated
interval multiple counts therefore apply directly. No endpoint loss is
hidden. Bad boundaries and dependent boundary pairs are actual images
of the proved bad-start and non-surjective joint-matrix sets. Their
membership tests use the original boundary arguments j+i and k+i.
The sets have their proved global cardinal bounds, including different
source and target word lengths S,T<=B and every containing cylinder.

ForcingExceptionLedger selects one threshold before B,Y,M,S,T, every
source set J in the actual boundary block, and all selected-prime data.
Under the literal finite cutoff, coprimeness and size conditions on q,R,
the surviving clean pair population is at least

  N*S_q - |J| - (K*T+1)*((N/Y)*S_q+|J|)
      - N^(19/10+epsilon) - N^(3/2+epsilon).

Here S_q=sum_{j in J}1/q_j and |R_j|<=K. The first proved exceptional
loss is |J| times the actual small-pivot target count, bounded using
|J|<=N. The second is the full raw-dependence pair count, charged ONCE
globally. No bound for either exceptional set is a theorem premise.
Source selection and the reciprocal source sum have not been replaced
by their desired asymptotics. Nearby-pair restrictions, selected-source
losses, reciprocal saddle comparison, full-value weighted upper profiles,
ordinary smooth short-interval input and final actual cost summations
remain to be completed.

Companion T19.16 now has an actual signed dyadic forcing cost
minorant with the clean arithmetic population and both exceptional
losses discharged. The logarithmic equivalent remains in progress.

WeightedPositiveForcingCostLower retains the full sum of the exact

The diagonal remains nonnegative and separate. SignedPrivateCleanCost
applies this to the SPECIFIED SignedPrivateField prime forcing. For an
actual clean pair with surjective joint raw-value matrix, the expected
target-indicator change is precisely its own signed mark rate, even
when source and target have different actual excesses. Multiplication
by the source's actual marginal gives their exact product. Neither the
target change cost nor a Palm identity is a theorem premise.

The Boolean indicator is explicitly identified with the prescribed raw
word. The physical one-bit transformation and uniform observation law
are the already proved original-prime-cylinder statements. The target
width is at most the source selected pivot by the field's actual privacy
condition. Thus the result is for the actual prescribed forcing map,
not an abstract coupling or a replacement target flip.

SignedDyadicCleanPairs translates a literal surviving boundary pair
injectively into the two zero-excess marks of one prescribed sign.
Its lifted pair count is EXACTLY the arithmetic pair count. Excluding
the actual bad-boundary and raw-dependent-pair sets guarantees both
marks are in the original retained field and the two raw words are
independent. Surjectivity also excludes equal boundaries, so no extra
diagonal loss or unproved separation premise is inserted.

Every survivor contributes (signedMarkRate L 0)^2. The source set can
be any subset J of the dyadic boundary block whose full maximal words
have pivots above Y. The target retained membership and joint matrix
condition are proved from survival; they are not separate cost inputs.
SignedCleanSourceData proves that the actual source's other pivots have
cardinality at most L+1, are above Y, and are coprime to the selected
first pivot. Privacy proves distinctness of all source pivots.

SignedDyadicCostLower combines these facts with the proved uniform
exception counts. For B*=L+E+2<=D*log N, 2B*<=Y<=log(N)^5 and all
such source sets J, one threshold preceding N,L,E,Y,J gives

 cost >= (signedMarkRate L 0)^2 *
  [ N*S_q - |J| - ((L+1)*(L+2)+1)*((N/Y)*S_q+|J|)
       - N^(19/10+epsilon) - N^(3/2+epsilon) ],

where S_q is the EXACT sum over j in J of 1/kappa(j). The cost on the
left is the full actual source-deleted signed coordinate cost on the
original retained dyadic field, with all original excess types through
E and both signs. No bound for either exceptional population, Palm
law, independent-word assumption or assumed cost lower rate remains
in this inequality. The exact reciprocal source sum still needs its
sharp saddle asymptotics and population restoration. The weighted
full-value upper profile and final logarithmic equivalent also remain
open. This finite actual lower bound is not counted as completed T19.16.

## Ordinary smooth source selection and the actual anchored cost

Stable ID: P1-ORDINARY-SMOOTH-NONANCHOR-SELECTION-COST. Companion T19.17 now has a constructive arithmetic small-pivot
selection for every anchor and an actual offsite cost minorant in terms

NonanchorPivotSelection defines ordinary candidate indices by the actual
largest prime factor of j+i, rather than the squarefree kernel or the
largest prime with odd valuation. The actual odd-valuation pivot is no
larger than that ordinary largest prime factor. If a source word has two
ordinary candidates at level Q, one lies outside EVERY prescribed anchor.
A simultaneous selector is constructed across the entire retained source
field, fixed before any random signs, and it selects a pivot <=Q at each
good source. At other sites it selects an arbitrary nonanchor index.

OrdinarySmoothSourcePopulation defines the actual good source set J:
dyadic boundaries with two ordinary candidates in the ACTUAL unsigned
word and with no pivot<=Z anywhere in the MAXIMAL support. It separately
defines the literal set H of sources missing the two ordinary candidates.
The exact finite deletion ledger gives

  N <= |J| + |H| + #badBoundaries(N,B,Z).

The last term already has its proved N^(9/10+epsilon) uniform bound.
The count |H| is left as the actual unresolved ordinary smooth short-
interval census, without calling it small or substituting a kernel census.

AnchoredSmallPivotSelection proves J is contained in the original
at-most-one-small-pivot retained field for Y<=Z. It constructs the chosen
small nonanchor ACTUAL private prime in each source for every admissible
arithmetic anchor rule. The exact source reciprocal sum then satisfies

  S_q >= |J|/Q.

Neither this reciprocal lower bound nor a small-pivot selector is a
premise in the final cost estimate: both are proved from the literal
ordinary candidates. All actual selected primes are positive.

CleanPairReciprocalLower factors the main reciprocal term together with
its collision loss before substitution:

  N*S_q - |J| - c*((N/Z)*S_q+|J|)
     = (1-c/Z)*N*S_q - (c+1)*|J|.

When c<=Z this coefficient is nonnegative, so S_q>=|J|/Q can be used
without reversing an inequality or bounding a negative reciprocal term
separately. This step keeps the small-pivot main scale.

AnchoredSmallPivotCostLower gives one threshold before all widths,
cutoffs, candidate levels Q, anchor rules, actual fields and templates.
Writing c=K*(K+1)+1 for an actual unsigned word of length K+1, if
K+1<=B<=D*log N, B<=Y<=Z<=log(N)^5, M>=2N+B and c<=Z, then

 actual offsite cost >= 2^(-2K) *
   [ (1-c/Z)*N*|J|/Q - (c+1)*|J|
       - N^(19/10+epsilon) - N^(3/2+epsilon) ].

This is an inequality for the actual prescribed anchored field. The
small-pivot choice is performed internally; clean-pair independence,
