## Uniform deterministic anchored obstruction under the ordinary census

Stable ID: P1-ANCHORED-OBSTRUCTION-UNDER-ORDINARY-CENSUS. Deterministic anchored obstruction proved conditional only on the independent OrdinaryCensusDensity predicate. Exact cutoff and every actual forcing/error step are internal; the ordinary census and randomized extension remain open. T19.17 remains in progress.

The deterministic-anchor part of companion T19.17 is now proved
under ONE explicit, independent ordinary source census. Every cutoff,

and arithmetic deletion is discharged. The census itself and the
randomized-orientation extension remain open, so T19.17 stays in progress.

LogFifthPivotCutoff keeps Z=floor(log(N)^5) exactly. For every fixed D
and t>0, one threshold before all B<=D*log N gives B^2+2<=t*Z.
For t<=1 this proves 2B<=Z, positive Z, and for K+1<=B the literal
collision coefficient c=K*(K+1)+1 satisfies c<=Z and c/Z<=t.
The floor and all quantifier orders are explicit; no fixed critical
length offset is used in this cutoff estimate.

PowerGap converts every strict exponent gap into an arbitrarily small
prescribed multiple. With epsilon=(1/10-a)/2 for 0<a<1/10,
AnchoredCostErrorScale proves, uniformly over every logarithmic word,

  N^(9/10+epsilon) <= (t/2)*N,
  (c+1)*N + N^(19/10+epsilon) + N^(3/2+epsilon)
       <= t*N^(2-a).

The polynomial collision endpoint cost is absorbed using the proved
uniform word-polynomial bound. The exact exponent 9/10 is kept separate
from the source/target-pair exponents 19/10 and 3/2.

AnchoredCostNormalization gives the finite comparison. If the retained
ordinary-candidate source fraction is at least 1-t, c/Z<=t, and the
three total errors cost at most t*N^2/Q, then the factored arithmetic
minorant is at least (1-3t)*N^2/Q. The exact squared source fraction
loses at most 2t. The source upper bound |J|<=N controls the negative
endpoint term in the correct direction.

AnchoredObstructionFromCensus applies this in the ORIGINAL unsigned
anchored field at Q=N^a and the exact natural Z. The sole additional
finite condition is that the literal sources missing two ordinary
candidates number at most (t/2)*N. The proved bad-pivot count controls
the other source loss. Thus one threshold, before every width, cutoff,
anchor rule, actual field and template, gives

  actual offsite cost >= (1-3t)*2^(-2K)*N^(2-a).

No forcing-cost bound, Palm law, independent-word law, small-pivot
choice, source reciprocal lower bound, cutoff limit or exceptional-set
estimate is an argument of this theorem.

input separately as OrdinaryCensusDensity(C,a): for every tau>0,

sources whose unsigned word of length L+i+1 lacks two ordinary

Its deduction from the Matomaki--Radziwill short-interval theorem is

Under this explicit independent arithmetic input, the theorem

proves the entire deterministic-anchor lower conclusion, uniformly

## Randomized orientation: full-private law and square-anchor scope test

Stable ID: P1-RANDOMIZED-PRIVATE-ORIENTATION-SCOPE. Fully private randomized conditional law proved internally for arbitrary finite auxiliary probabilities. The original one-small retained population admits a square-anchor scope counterexample to dropping full privacy. The numerical lower bound is not refuted; randomized aggregation and ordinary census remain open. T19.17 remains in progress.

Companion T19.17 gains an exact scope test for the randomized
conditional-law paragraph and a proof of that law under the essential
fully private hypothesis. This does not refute the printed numerical
obstruction. Its randomized cost aggregation and ordinary source census
remain open, so the numbered result stays in progress.

The randomized paragraph follows a restriction to sources whose entire
maximal support has pivots above Y0. That restriction must be retained
when asserting that fairness of g(U,xi) gives the conditional source law.
Extending the assertion to the WHOLE original one-small-pivot retained
population is false. The distinction is now checked in the actual model.

OddPivotSpecialValues proves the exact actual pivots of every square
and prime. RandomOrientationSquareAnchor uses the concrete word (4,5),
start 5, maximal width 2, cutoff Y=4, dyadic parameter N=3 and prime
cylinder M=8. Its square anchor has pivot 1; its only other pivot is
the private prime 5>4. The word is proved to belong to the original
at-most-one-small-pivot retained population and its unsigned event has
actual probability 1/2.

Take independent fair auxiliary xi and g(U,xi)=xi, which is fair for
a uniform raw source word, and even for each fixed original sample.
The actual map changes only private prime 5 and sets the nonanchor
source value to its prescribed template plus xi. The square 4 keeps
raw bit zero under EVERY sample. Consequently the forced unsigned
start event holds exactly when xi=1, with probability 1/2 instead of
one. The theorem not_full_conditional_law explicitly refutes the full
conditional-observable identity for this map, using the event itself
as an observable. This is a local conditional-law scope counterexample,
not an asymptotic counterexample to the numerical lower bound.

FairBinaryMixture handles an ARBITRARY finite auxiliary probability,
not merely uniform auxiliary bits. A fair F2-valued function of the
original uniform source word and independent auxiliary randomness gives
the exact half-and-half mixture of its two outputs for every real
observable. No independence of g from the source is required.

RandomizedPrivatePalmForcing requires every ORIGINAL raw source
coordinate to have its actual private prime basis vector. It changes
only those prime coordinates and hits the target unsigned orbit for
every sample and auxiliary draw. For every fixed background chart,
uniform source coordinates and the fair orientation give exactly the
equal mixture of the two specified signed forcings. Averaging the
actual prime-cylinder chart then proves the complete unsigned
conditional law for EVERY real observable of the full sample. Its
exact event rate is 2^(-(m-1)) for a nonempty source word of length m.
The weighted conditional identity and preservation of every nonselected
prime are also proved. The fairness input is solely the prescribed
orientation condition; no Palm law or probability value is a premise.

Thus the random-orientation paragraph is valid on the fully private
good sources used in the lower count. On other retained sources one
must keep the unforced anchor compatible with the imposed orientation,
for example by the already proved anchor-preserving map. Merely
requiring an unconstrained fair sign is insufficient there. The
original deterministic-anchor theorem and its conditional obstruction
are unchanged. A global hybrid randomized field and the half-factor
cost aggregation still need their own formalization.

P1-MATH-0189 records this SCOPE CLARIFICATION as an improvement: it
prevents dropping the preceding full-private restriction, rather than
declaring the printed T19.17 numerical conclusion false. The sole
existing confirmed statement correction remains P1-MATH-0162.
There are 188 improvements and one statement-scope correction. Coverage
stays 88 proved and 69 conditional out of 167, with ten incomplete
results. No source-manuscript bytes, external axioms, dependency or
compiler versions are changed. Palomar remains deferred.

## Actual randomized clean-target cost and quarter-flip selection

Stable ID: P1-RANDOMIZED-ACTUAL-CLEAN-PIVOT-COST. Actual randomized clean-target cost and ordinary quarter-flip choice proved internally for arbitrary finite independent auxiliary laws. Global hybrid field, source aggregation and ordinary source census remain open. T19.17 remains in progress.

Companion T19.17 gains the actual randomized clean-target cost
formula and a quarter-flip ordinary source choice, with an arbitrary
independent finite auxiliary probability. The global hybrid field,
source aggregation and final randomized obstruction remain in progress.

IndependentFiniteProbability constructs the literal product law from
arbitrary normalized finite real weights. It proves weighted Fubini,
both exact marginals and the uniform/weighted expectation interchange.
No uniformity or separate nonempty instance is imposed on the auxiliary
law. RawAuxiliaryObservation then derives the actual joint uniform
source/target word law with that independent auxiliary law from the
surjective original raw matrix. An assumed independent-word probability
law is not substituted for the original prime model.

RandomizedSourceFlip uses the actual correction

  delta_i(U,xi)=U_i+b_i+g(U,xi).

For any two different original source indices, their correction bits
sum to the original fair parity. The orientation may depend arbitrarily
on U and xi. Weighted finite expectation therefore proves that one
candidate has flip probability theta_i>=1/4. If the actual source has
two ordinary Q-smooth candidate indices, one such candidate is selected
among them. This local cost selection does NOT require fairness of g;
the fully private Palm law requires the separate fairness hypothesis
proved and scoped at P1-MATH-0189.

RandomizedCleanPivotWordCost connects this calculation to the actual

## Independent short-interval input implies the literal ordinary source census

Stable ID: P1-MR2016-COR6-LOG-SMOOTH-INPUT. Unformalized primary source: Matomaki--Radziwill2016, Corollary6, Annals183, p.1019, DOI10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.6. CorollarySixLogInput is an explicit theorem premise; its full deduction of the actual ordinary source census is proved internally.

The independent ordinary smooth source census in companion T19.17

all interval, exponent, density and moving-critical-width comparisons
proved in Lean. The analytic input itself is NOT proved or installed
as an axiom. T19.17 remains in progress pending its final printed
parameter and nominal-scale specialization.

Published source: K. Matomaki and M. Radziwill, Multiplicative functions
in short intervals, Annals of Mathematics 183 (2016), 1015-1056, Corollary 6,
p. 1019, DOI 10.4007/annals.2016.183.3.6. The primary published PDF was
checked on 4 November 2026:
https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v183-n3-p06-p.pdf
For a fixed positive smoothness parameter, that result gives a
positive-density relative smooth-number count in almost all intervals
whose length tends to infinity. We use only its fixed u=2/a logarithmic
specialization and the positivity of the associated limiting density.

OrdinaryShortIntervalCensusInput makes the needed weakening explicit.
RelativeDensityInput(psi,a,rho) says that for every delta>0, the number
of j<X whose actual ordinary smooth-candidate count in indices
0,...,psi(j), at threshold j^(a/2), differs from rho*psi(j) by more
than delta*psi(j), is at most delta*X for sufficiently large X.
The interval is inclusive and its actual candidate set is the
previously defined ordinaryIndices, with no odd-kernel substitution.

For EVERY natural psi tending to infinity and every rho>0, Lean
proves that this input implies TwoCandidateDensity: the number of
j<X with fewer than two actual candidates is o(X). The proof removes
a finite initial segment where psi is small, compares the remaining
failure to the relative-error set and absorbs the finite initial
count at the specified density tolerance. All these losses and
threshold quantifiers are explicit.

LogarithmicOrdinaryCensusBridge uses

  psi(j)=floor(log(j)/(4*log(2))),

proves psi tends to infinity, and defines CorollarySixLogInput(a) as
the existence of a positive rho with that relative-density input.
The smaller logarithmic interval is permitted by the published
corollary and suffices for the actual word.

Uniformly for every L with |L-log(N)/log(2)|<=C, every original dyadic
boundary j and sufficiently large N, psi(j)<=L. The threshold precedes
L and j. OrdinaryCandidateMonotonicity proves exact finite candidate
cardinality monotonicity in BOTH word width and smoothness cutoff.
It also proves j^(a/2)<=N^a for j<=2N and N>=2, using j<=N^2.
Thus every short-interval candidate pair is an actual candidate pair
in either unsigned source word K=L+i, i=0,1.

Every missing-candidate ORIGINAL boundary lies in the literal bad
prefix set below 2N. Its cardinality is bounded by that entire prefix
set. Applying the natural-density estimate at 2N with tolerance tau/2
gives exactly tau*N. There is no endpoint or unrecorded translation
loss. Consequently CorollarySixLogInput(a) implies the independent
OrdinaryCensusDensity(C,a) for every fixed C and a>0, with no forcing,
anchor, probability, cost or reciprocal sum in either analytic input.

## Homogeneity of actual factors from exact lowest and highest total degrees

Stable ID: p1:internal:homogeneous-factor-degrees. Unconditional multivariate polynomial and formal-series degrees. Domain assumptions are confined to the product identities; no homogeneous factor or geometric input is assumed.

A needed algebraic step for the actual projective identification is now proved: every factor of a nonzero homogeneous multivariate polynomial over an integral domain is homogeneous, with degree equal to its own actual total degree. No homogeneous-factor decomposition is assumed.

The proof compares the highest and lowest actual total degrees. Embedding a multivariate polynomial into formal power series gives its lowest-degree order. For a nonzero polynomial, this order is at most its total degree; for a homogeneous polynomial it equals the homogeneous degree. Conversely, equality of the series order and the polynomial total degree forces every nonzero coefficient to have that degree, proving homogeneity.

In an integral domain, actual polynomial total degrees add under a nonzero product, and formal-series orders add exactly. If the product is homogeneous, the two sums coincide. The individual lower-degree orders are bounded by the individual upper degrees, so each pair is equal. This proves both factors homogeneous, using only the checked degree/order identities and finite coefficient extensionality. The preparatory order and homogeneity criteria work already over commutative semirings; the no-zero-divisor domain assumption is used at the product step.

## Triangular-power divisibility for filtered evaluation determinants

Stable ID: p1:internal:filtered-evaluation-determinant-divisibility. Internal finite algebraic proof from the injective determinant expansion, distinct-degree sum bound and principal-ideal quotient. Motivated by Heath-Brown arXiv:1010.6217v3 Section6, printedpp12-13; the sharp b>=2 count remains unproved.

FilteredEvaluationDeterminantDivisibility.evaluation_triangular_dvd proves p^(k*(k-1)/2) divides the determinant of the actual finite evaluation matrix C*V when every entry of row r of V is divisible by p^r. The coefficient matrix C is arbitrary. The proof retains only injective monomial selections in the internally proved determinant expansion. Distinct natural degrees have sum at least0+1+...+(k-1), and the row-wise power divisibilities give the corresponding determinant divisor.

The theorem works over every commutative ring, for any element p, without primality, a domain hypothesis or analytic convergence. Its finite truncation scope is explicit: it does not yet construct the required representation for actual smooth curve points. determinant_congruence_dvd proves that entrywise congruence modulo any d implies determinant congruence modulo d, using the principal-ideal quotient. evaluation_congruent_dvd consequently preserves the triangular divisor when the actual matrix differs from its filtered representation by entries divisible by that same power.

The six new theorems supply a finite algebraic core of the p-adic determinant step in the remaining Heath-Brown argument. Constructing a compatible polynomial or truncated-series representation on each actual smooth residue class, choosing primes, controlling sizes, building auxiliary forms and finishing the global count remain separate open work. The sharp b>=2 Heath-Brown property is not asserted. The b=1 case and non-geometric input remain internally proved.

Stable ID: p1:internal:bivariate-nilpotent-implicit-polynomial. Internal finite implicit-function construction from a truncated polynomial parameter, nilpotent root existence and uniqueness. No branch representation, point count or analytic convergence is assumed.

BivariateNilpotentImplicitFunction.exists_polynomial_implicit proves an actual finite implicit-function theorem over every commutative ring R. If I^N=0, P(a,b) lies in I and the outer derivative at(a,b) is a unit modulo I, there is one polynomial q in R[T] such that every actual root P(x,y)=0 with x-a and y-b in I satisfies y=q(x-a). The polynomial is constructed internally and precedes all point choices. No branch representation is assumed, and no monicity, domain, characteristic or analytic convergence hypothesis is used.

The construction uses R[T]/(T^N), represented by the actual AdjoinRoot ring, with ideal J generated by the image of I and T. NilpotentPolynomialParameter proves J^(N+N)=0, exact evaluation at every nilpotent t in I, transport of J into I, and existence and evaluation of polynomial representatives. The transformed equation is exactly P(a+T,Y). Its value and derivative modulo J are transported from the original point. The internally checked nilpotent simple-root theorem constructs a root in this ring. Evaluation gives actual roots over every t in I; the separately proved uniqueness in the residue class identifies all actual curve points with this fixed polynomial.

## Fixed dyadic prime family with uniform integer avoidance

Stable ID: p1:internal:dyadic-prime-cover. Bertrand is proved in the pinned Mathlib and compiled locally. The prime family and avoidance conclusion are constructed, not added as unproved inputs.

DyadicPrimeCover.uniform_pool proves that for every positive integer P and fixed m there is one finite family T of exactly m distinct primes, all in(P,2^m*P], with sum at most m*2^m*P, such that every nonzero signed integer n with |n|<P^m is avoided by at least one prime of T. The same family works simultaneously for every such n. No prime-density, interval-supply, prime-family or coverage premise is assumed.

exists_pool constructs the family by choosing one Bertrand prime in each successive dyadic interval and proves distinctness, the exact cardinality and product>=P^m. pool_sum_bound gives the explicit sum budget. exists_nondividing proves that if all distinct primes divided n, their product would divide |n| and contradict its strict size bound. The only new Mathlib module is the already proved Bertrand theorem, compiled locally under the pinned compiler; no dependency download is needed.

This is a checked alternative to the interval prime supply in the local determinant method: fixed m allows a larger constant interval(P,2^m*P] without changing the final power of P. Applying it to the actual product of projective denominators and derivative, proving that product nonzero outside controlled exceptions, and deriving its size bound remain open. The final smooth-class cover and sharp exponent assembly are not claimed.

## Divisor-grouped square ranges and exact finite parabola counts

Stable ID: p1:internal:parabolic-conic-finite-count. The gcd grouping gives a residue modulus whose square is at least the original modulus. This proves the finite bound; geometric and asymptotic consequences remain explicit next obligations.

SquareCongruenceRangeCount proves a signed square-root bound for actual integer square congruences. If M>0, every z in an actual finite population satisfies M|(z^2-base^2), and every square-value difference is at most M*R with R>=0, then the population has at most 2*tau(M)*(sqrt(R)+1) elements. No squarefree, coprime, primitivity or shift-size condition is imposed.

The proof groups z by g=gcd(M,z-base). Exact congruence cancellation proves M/g divides z+base. Within one actual gcd fibre, both g and M/g divide every pairwise difference, so the common residue modulus max(g,M/g) has square at least M. An injective exact quotient map gives the finite interval count. For nonnegative z the coordinate-span square is at most the square-value span, and division by this modulus yields sqrt(R)+1 points per fibre. The gcd image consists of actual divisors of M. Passing through absolute values retains both signs with multiplicity at most two.

ParabolicConicFiniteCount applies this to the actual conic square coordinate W=2*c*y+b*x+e. When the discriminant is zero, c!=0 and beta=2*b*e-4*c*d!=0, that coordinate is injective on actual integer zeros, and W^2=beta*x+gamma. Consequently every finite population of zeros with |x|<=H has cardinality at most 2*tau(|beta|)*(sqrt(2*H)+1), with no bound on y and with both coordinate signs and all axis points retained. The width estimate uses the actual square-value identity and the exact modulus |beta|, rather than bounding W by coefficient height.

This is the exact finite arithmetic bound for the parabolic branch. The eventual uniform N^(1/2+epsilon) estimate still needs the elementary divisor budget, and actual geometric polynomials still need their leading-coordinate choice and non-degeneracy supplied internally. Original coefficient normalization is also separate. These consequences are not yet claimed. One absolute positive constant precedes the degree, scale, coefficients and population. grid_geometric_count specializes to the entire actual grid. The equation coefficients have no height restriction.

Its checked upper bound is K*D^6*(Nat.log2(N)+1)^2*N^(1/D), with K chosen before D and N. It proves the actual global count on the sheared box for height at most N^(32*D^3), with outer degreeD and first partial degree at mostD. All derivative/denominator exceptions are included. The exact resulting degree powers are D^2 for the residue-class factor, D for auxiliary intersection, D^3 for the avoidance count and D^6 for the prime scale, giving D^12 overall; all four logarithmic factors are retained.

For unrestricted original coefficients, the bounded shear and post-shear interpolation from checkpoint405 give the actual small-height presentation whenever the population has more than D^2 points. The shear is injective and expands the integer box by at most D+1. Populations of size at mostD^2 are absorbed directly. This completes the previously pending weaker polynomial-degree estimate, with no geometric or counting input left in these canonical statements.

## Anchored prime confinement at every fixed arity

Stable ID: p1:internal:fixed-arity-anchored-confinement. The prime supports are chosen minimal supports anchored in one actual window. No higher-arity claim about whole prime rows or automatic inheritance of recovery exclusion is made.

AnchoredPhysicalPrimeGroups replaces the three-block whole-prime-row argument by prime supports chosen through one distinguished actual window. Each active large prime is assigned one minimal recovery support containing its unique anchor position. Supports may involve any fixed number of other blocks. The actual groups are globally coprime, divide every value in their chosen support and cover every large odd prime of each active anchor value.

For recovery radius s>=1, bounded support-pool incidence gives at most supportBound(s,t,t-1) distinct groups through any anchor position. This proof uses minimal chosen supports, not the assertion that an entire row remains minimal after deleting a position. In particular it does not remove the essential radius-at-most-two restriction from the earlier whole-row incidence lemma.

Erasing only the anchor positions of the large groups costs at most one dimension per group, independent of the arity. Two active positions survive whenever the original physical dimension exceeds the number of large groups and the anchor projection is injective. Their actual large odd kernels are each at most Y^supportBound(s,t,t-1). Recovery exclusion and groups refer throughout to the original subspace; no recovery property is assumed to survive erasure.

OffsetNonalignmentFrom records exactly the required anchor/other-block condition, restricted to active positions. No source/source nonalignment is imposed. AnchoredPhysicalGroupCount proves, for every fixed s and positive tau,epsilon, a uniform threshold before all critical windows, actual starts and physical subspaces such that the number of groups larger than N^tau is at most epsilon*(L+1). The internally proved polynomial confinement is applied separately to the s possible receiving blocks. Every group retains its own index even when projected offset pairs coincide.

DenseAnchoredKernelWitness combines these facts. For arbitrary fixed arity s+1, actual dense physical dimension eta*L, recovery exclusion at radius s, active anchor/other nonalignment and injective anchor projection imply two actual values whose kernel product is at most N^(2*tau*supportBound(s,t,t-1)). Other projections may be dependent, and no nonalignment among the other blocks is required.

FixedArityPhysicalRelationRegularization and FixedArityPhysicalSubspaceRegularization generalize the checked dimension budgets to every fixed radius d>=1 and arity at most d+1. The recovery order is selected before the window length and all physical data. The first theorem lifts the effective kernel when its projections are injective; the second constructs a fresh recovery subspace inside any prescribed physical subspace and preserves each individual injective projection as well as previously erased coordinates.

These are internally proved arithmetic and regularization tools. Applying them to all actual old-source configurations, transporting indices and proving the complete dense-target conclusion remain further work. Main15.2 stays conditional. TruncatedAffineDegree uses b=min(D,L+1) for the vertical auxiliary basis and J=b-1. It proves2<=b, J<D and A+J<=5L for A=3L+1. Otherwise log((D+1)N)<=3L gives the bounded root exp(3), so one fixed absolute prime threshold suffices. This removes the avoidable extra degree factor in the auxiliary intersection budget without altering any Bezout count.

The strict inequality uses65 versus64, retaining the original interpolation and bad-integer height budgets. The fixed elementary bound logP<=P/2 pays the rounding allowance. Prime supply, averaging, height avoidance and determinant hypotheses are all internally supplied; no new prime-distribution input is assumed.

FifthDegreeUniformAffineCount combines this prime scale with the truncated auxiliary basis and the existing exact finite smooth-class and averaged-prime counts. The principal product is bounded by640*K*D^5*L^2*N^(1/D); the fixed exceptional integer points are absorbed separately. FifthDegreeUniformFieldCount transports through rational presentations, nongeometric point bounds and scalar descent to every characteristic-zero field, including D>N and arbitrary finite point populations. No complex embedding of the original coefficient field is used.

FifthGrowingDegreePlaneCount proves the new uniform power cap, real scaled cutoff and general growing cap below1/5. Its threshold precedes every degree, coefficient field and equation. Stable ID: p1:internal:fixed-gap-interpolation-coordinates. Preparatory finite row-rank and polynomial-coordinate tools only. The actual curve rank gap, improved height presentation and generic point-count application remain open.

RectangularPolynomialCoordinates supplies actual monomial coordinates over every commutative coefficient ring. Both linear maps and every coefficient/outside-support identity are proved. The coordinate implementation can retain a positive-dimensional family of multiples when an interpolation degree is enlarged; it does not discard that freedom by selecting only one kernel direction.

These are preparatory algebraic ingredients for a sharper height presentation. ## Finite Rolle zero populations and a recursive Chebyshev criterion

Stable ID: p1:internal:finite-rolle-recursive-chebyshev. Finite Rolle and recursive normalized-pivot zero counts are internal. Classical partial-Wronskian, curve-piece and smooth-parametrization bridges remain open.

The finite zero-counting core for the real-analytic BCN route is now internally proved. FiniteRolleZeros constructs one actual derivative zero in every gap between consecutive points of any given finite zero population inside an open real interval. The construction uses the increasing finite enumeration and Rolle theorem, proves the constructed derivative zeros are distinct and retains their interval membership. It needs only continuity of the original function on that interval. There is no assumed finiteness or cardinality bound for the whole zero set.

The finite derivative inequality and its iteration are proved separately. A boundk on all finite derivative-zero populations yields at mostk+1 original zeros. If every iterated derivative through ordern is continuous and the actualnth derivative is nowhere zero, every finite original zero population has cardinality at mostn. The casesn=0, empty populations and arbitrary open intervals are included.

RecursiveChebyshev gives a concrete recursive pivot criterion. For an actual finite family, divide its tail by the first function and differentiate. Admissible requires differentiability of the current functions, nonvanishing of the current first function, and the same conditions on the smaller normalized derivative family. These are actual regularity and pivot properties; no zero-count estimate is a field or premise. The normalized finite-sum identity and its actual derivative are proved, with all nonvanishing divisions and interval restrictions explicit. Induction using the finite Rolle construction proves every combination with nonzero coefficient vector has fewer zeros than the family size. Evaluation at any sufficiently large actual finite set is therefore injective, and vanishing there forces every coefficient to be zero.

This is a preparatory recursive-pivot form, not yet the classical partial-Wronskian criterion used in BCN. The determinant identities connecting those pivots to the actual partial Wronskians, their nonvanishing on geometric curve pieces, the bounded number of such pieces, smooth parametrizations and the final sharp point count remain subsequent obligations. No new proof ofBCN, full main13.4 or original13.5 is claimed. The current generic plane theorem remains the internally proved cubic degree estimate, with fulla<1/3 growing range. The complete main optimal scalar laws and unconditional dense graph clause ofT1.7 remain unchanged.

The primary BCN author version arXiv2302.04209v2, Sections2-5, was read directly to identify this outstanding real-analytic route. Its theorem is not used as an axiom or a proved input. The pinned Mathlib Rolle and finite-sum differentiation APIs supply the basic calculus, and no additional cache or dependency is downloaded.

## Actual polynomial tangent Wronskians with triangular degree budgets

Stable ID: p1:internal:polynomial-tangent-wronskian-degree. Actual tangent differentiation, curve-ideal preservation and polynomial Wronskian degree budgets are internal; analytic and geometric nonvanishing/counting bridges remain open.

The actual polynomial tangent operator and its Wronskian degree estimates are now internally proved over every commutative coefficient ring. PolynomialTangentDegree definesL_P(Q)=P_y*Q_x-P_x*Q_y on two-variable multivariate polynomials. It proves additivity, the product rule, annihilation of constants and ofP, and the exact identityL_P(PQ)=P*L_P(Q). Thus the defining curve ideal is preserved by the actual operator; no abstract tangency claim is assumed.

The partial derivative degree bound is proved directly from the coefficient formula and finite support, including zero polynomials and arbitrary coefficient cancellation. It yieldsdegL_P(Q)<=degP+degQ anddegL_P^n(Q)<=degQ+n*degP. No irreducibility, characteristic-zero or analytic premise is needed for these algebraic allowances.

PolynomialTangentWronskian defines the genuine determinant of the actual repeated tangent derivatives. A general multivariate polynomial matrix lemma bounds its determinant degree by the sum of its row allowances, including arbitrary commutative rings, signed permutation terms and the empty matrix. Forn actual basis candidates of degree at mostk, the tangent Wronskian has degree at most the exact row sumsum_(i<n)(k+i*degP)=n*k+(n*(n-1)/2)*degP. The loosern*(k+n*degP) bound used by BCN Proposition5 follows as a separate checked theorem. The triangular allowance is retained rather than replacing every row by its maximum.

The primary BCN author version arXiv2302.04209v2 Section3, Definition3 and Proposition5, was rechecked against these actual formulas. These proofs concern degrees of genuine polynomials and determinants. They do not assert that a partial Wronskian is nonzero on the curve or that every curve piece has the recursive pivot property. The classical analytic normalization identity, nonvanishing/independence argument, finite exceptional curve pieces, smooth parametrizations and final sharp point count remain subsequent obligations. NoBCN or main13.4 coverage is claimed. The current generic plane bound remains cubic, with fulla<1/3 growing range; complete main optimal scalar laws and the unconditional denseT1.7 graph clause are unchanged.

## Classical Polya Chebyshev criterion from actual Wronskian identities

Stable ID: p1:internal:classical-polya-wronskian-criterion. The classical smooth partial-Wronskian Chebyshev criterion is internal. Actual curve-trajectory and nonvanishing/decomposition/parametrization bridges remain open.

The classical partial-Wronskian Chebyshev criterion is now internally proved for actual smooth real functions. Forn functions on an open real interval, assumeC-infinity regularity and that the genuine determinant Wronskian of every nonempty initial family is nowhere zero there. Every combination with a nonzero coefficient vector then has strictly fewer thann distinct zeros. Coefficient recovery fromn actual sample points and injectivity of their evaluation map are also proved. The zero bound is a conclusion, not an input, and no externally asserted Polya theorem is assumed.

AnalyticWronskianProduct constructs the actual iterated derivative matrix and its lower triangular common-factor multiplication matrix. The finite Leibniz sum is proved to equal the full matrix product, including its exact truncation. Its diagonal is the common factor, hence multiplication of every function bya multiplies the determinant bya^n. All regularity assumptions are explicit pointwise finite-orderContDiffAt conditions; no formal differential operator is substituted for the actual derivatives.

AnalyticWronskianNormalization proves open-set congruence for the genuine Wronskians and the exact first-column identity for a family beginning with1. Dividing every function by the original first function givesW(f_0,...,f_n)=f_0^(n+1)*W((f_1/f_0)',...,(f_n/f_0)'). Every division is confined to the actual open nonvanishing set, and every actual derivative congruence is justified there. No global extension of a quotient identity is presumed.

PolyaChebyshevCriterion applies that normalization identity to every actual initial family. Nonvanishing of their Wronskians supplies all recursive pivots, and smoothness is retained after each division and derivative. The already proved finite Rolle induction then yields the strict zero bound and finite evaluation consequences. The proof needsC-infinity rather than real analyticity. Empty families, empty intervals, zero coefficients in all but the first position and all finite endpoint cases are included.

The primary BCN author version arXiv2302.04209v2 Section2, Definitions1-2 and the stated Polya theorem, was rechecked. This closes that classical calculus ingredient. The polynomial tangent Wronskian degrees remain internal fromP1-MATH-0499. Matching them to actual curve trajectories, proving the relevant polynomial Wronskians do not vanish identically, bounding the exceptional pieces, constructing controlled smooth parametrizations and the final sharp point estimate remain subsequent obligations. Complete main13.4 BCN and original13.5 are not promoted. Current generic point counting remains the cubic-degree theorem with completea<1/3 range.

Stable ID: p1:internal:actual-tangent-curve-piece-zeros. Actual trajectory smoothness, tangent/classical Wronskian agreement and one-piece finite zero populations are internal. Global trajectory and exceptional decomposition obligations remain open.

Actual polynomial tangent trajectories are now connected to the classical Chebyshev criterion. PolynomialEvaluationDerivative proves the finite sum of evaluated formal partials is the genuine directional derivative of multivariate polynomial evaluation. The chain rule is obtained by polynomial induction from constants, addition and multiplication by a variable. PolynomialTangentTrajectory defines the actual polynomial vector field(P_y,-P_x) and its componentwise ordinary differential equation on an open real set. The equation itself impliesC-infinity regularity: start from the continuous coordinate functions supplied by their derivatives, then bootstrap each finite order using smooth polynomial evaluation of the velocity. Smoothness is not an extra trajectory hypothesis. Along every such actual trajectory, the real derivative ofQ equals the evaluation ofL_P(Q). The open-set congruence argument then proves every iterated derivative equals the corresponding actual formal tangent iterate. TangentCurvePieceZeros turns nonvanishing of the actual polynomial initial Wronskians along one trajectory into the classical initial-Wronskian premise. Thus every nontrivial combination has fewer zeros than the family size on the parameter interval. The result also counts actual distinct plane points in the image: choose one parameter for each finite population point; equality of selected parameters forces equality of those points, so the selected parameter map is injective. The trajectory itself need not be injective. This retains every original population point and does not replace them by a differently sized set.

## Local linear independence and genuine Wronskian nonvanishing

Stable ID: p1:internal:local-independence-wronskian-nonvanishing. The local smooth Wronskian nonvanishing argument is internal. Local independence of actual curve polynomial restrictions and finite polynomial exceptional bounds remain subsequent obligations.

A complete local linear-independence route to actual Wronskian nonvanishing is now internally proved for smooth real functions. LocalLinearIndependence.Independent requires that every nonzero coefficient vector gives a combination that is nonzero somewhere on every nonempty open subinterval. This is explicitly stronger than mere linear independence on the whole interval; the proof does not incorrectly infer it from global smooth independence.

Restriction preserves this local property, and the first family function is nonzero at some point of every nonempty interval. Dividing the tail by the first function and differentiating preserves local independence wherever the first function is nowhere zero. Indeed, a putative vanishing derivative combination makes the original normalized combination constant by the actual derivative-zero theorem. Adding the negative constant as the first coefficient then gives a forbidden original vanishing combination. Every coefficient vector and nonzero divisor is constructed explicitly.

LocalWronskianNonvanishing proves by induction that the genuine classical Wronskian is nonzero somewhere on each nonempty open subinterval. Continuity at an actual nonzero first-function value constructs a smaller interval where division is valid. The normalized derivative tail is smooth and locally independent there, so induction supplies its nonzero Wronskian value. The already proved determinant normalization identity then gives the required original nonzero value. Empty families are included, with determinant1.

This argument supplies the local function-theoretic step without an unformalized analytic Wronskian theorem. Its intended application to actual curve polynomial restrictions still has to establish the displayed local independence. That requires the actual nonstationary trajectory image and the finite Bezout/degree argument; neither is silently assumed here. Nonzero values on every subinterval alone also do not assert finiteness of a general smooth Wronskian zero set. Polynomial nondivisibility and finite exceptional bounds remain separate geometric obligations.

The primary BCN author version arXiv2302.04209v2 Section3 Lemma6 was rechecked for this distinction. The polynomial degree budgets, classical Chebyshev criterion, actual trajectory derivative identities and one-piece point count are already internal. Actual global trajectory existence/coverage, polynomial Wronskian nondivisibility, controlled exceptional pieces, bounded smooth parametrizations and the final sharp count remain open. NoBCN or original13.5 promotion is made; the current generic plane count remains cubic with fulla<1/3 range.

## Actual curve polynomial independence and finite Wronskian exceptions

Stable ID: p1:internal:curve-polynomial-wronskian-exceptions. Actual polynomial restriction independence and Wronskian nondivisibility/exceptional bounds are internal for a given independent low-degree family and genuine nonstationary trajectory. Concrete monomial and global geometric assemblies remain open.

The actual polynomial-restriction independence and tangent Wronskian nondivisibility argument is now internally connected to finite Bezout. NonstationaryTangentImage proves the actual trajectory position map is continuous. A nonzero coordinate velocity at one interval point prevents its image from being a singleton: a singleton image would make each coordinate constant, contradicting its actual derivative. The connected image therefore has infinitely many distinct points. A trajectory nonstationary everywhere has this property on every nonempty subinterval. The defining polynomial is also proved constant along the actual trajectory, and an actual zero at one parameter propagates throughout its interval.

MvPlaneBezout transports the existing finite Bezout theorem into actualFin2 multivariate coordinates over every infinite field. The real point coordinate map, its injection, exact evaluation and exact total degrees are all proved. An infinite actual common-zero population forces polynomial divisibility. Thus a nonzero polynomial of strictly smaller degree cannot vanish on an infinite population of an irreducible curve. No analytic identity principle or geometric count interface replaces that finite argument.

CurvePolynomialWronskianNonvanishing applies these facts to an actual finite polynomial family of degree at mostk<degP. Its polynomial coefficient map is required to be injective in the explicit form that every nonzero vector gives a nonzero polynomial combination; concrete monomial families are a subsequent instantiation. Every nonempty subinterval has infinitely many actual curve points, so finite Bezout supplies a point where any such combination is nonzero. This proves the precise local linear independence of the real restrictions rather than assuming it. Actual trajectory smoothness and the local Wronskian theorem then supply a nonzero value of the genuine polynomial tangent Wronskian on the curve. Consequently the defining irreducible polynomial does not divide that Wronskian.

For every finite actual population satisfying both equations, the complete resulting exceptional bound is proved:S.card<=D*(n*k+(n*(n-1)/2)*D), whereD=degP andn is the actual family size. It retains the triangular derivative budget, all original real points and ordinary irreducibility. Only one given genuine nonstationary trajectory interval is needed to establish this global polynomial nondivisibility. No trajectory-existence theorem or global coverage is asserted without proof.

The primary BCN author version arXiv2302.04209v2 Section3 Lemma6 was rechecked. Concrete ordered monomial-prefix families, controlled unions of their exceptional zeros, global trajectory existence/coverage, the number of pieces, bounded smooth parametrizations and the final sharp point count remain subsequent obligations. The current generic point estimate is still the internally proved cubic bound with fulla<1/3 growing range. CompleteBCN/main13.4 and original13.5 are not promoted.

The ordered monomial families in the sharp-degree curve argument are now concrete and internally complete. ## Exact normalized graph derivative numerators and external recurrence sign correction

Stable ID: p1:internal:exact-normalized-graph-derivative-numerators. Every positive-order actual derivative on a supplied normalized x-chart now has its internally constructed rational polynomial formula and degree bound. The external mixed-term sign erratum is separate from P1 statement-scope corrections.

RationalTangentNumerator constructs the exact polynomial quotient recurrence for the normalized graph operator L_x = partial_x - (P_x/P_y) partial_y. Index n corresponds to derivative order n+1 and denominator P_y^(2n+1). Its recurrence is N_next = P_y L_P(N) - e N L_P(P_y), where L_P = P_y partial_x - P_x partial_y and e=2n+1. The expanded mixed term has a minus sign. The construction works over any commutative ring, and its actual polynomial numerator has total degree at most deg(Q)+2 deg(P)(n+1). No nonzero numerator is presumed.

GraphTangentEvaluation defines an actual normalized trajectory with first-coordinate derivative one, second-coordinate derivative -P_x/P_y and explicit nonvanishing of P_y at every parameter. It proves the actual evaluation chain rule and constancy of the curve equation. IteratedGraphDerivative verifies the quotient differentiation algebra, the derivative of every numerator quotient, the complete open-chart iterated derivative identity, and the positive-order statement: for every j>=1 there is an actual polynomial N of degree at most deg(Q)+2 deg(P)j such that the j-th real derivative of Q along the chart is N/P_y^(2j-1). These are ordinary real derivatives of the actual functions, not supplied derivative identities. No existence of such a normalized chart is asserted by this checkpoint.

The primary author version of Binyamini--Cluckers--Novikov, arXiv:2302.04209v2, Section 4 Proposition 8, equation (21), was checked both in the official PDF and official HTML. Its displayed expanded recurrence has a plus sign in the P_y P_x partial_y(N) term, whereas the stated L_x definition and quotient rule require a minus sign. A kernel-checked polynomial counterexample uses P=x+y+xy, Q=y and the curve point (0,0), where P_y=1: the corrected second numerator evaluates to 2, while the displayed plus-sign expression evaluates to 0. This is recorded in docs/LITERATURE_ERRATA.md as a separate external-reference erratum. It is not a third false P1 statement or a claim that BCN's theorem is false. The corrected recurrence retains the stated degree allowance.

This is the first normalized coordinate orientation. Swapped coordinates, existence of actual normalized charts, finite derivative-control exceptions, global controlled piece counts, bounded parametrizations, the final quadratic-degree plane estimate and higher-dimensional projection remain separate. Full main13.4/13.5 remain unresolved. The current generic plane theorem is still cubic with the full a<1/3 growing-degree range.

## Complete finite two-orientation graph-control exceptions with quadratic budget

Stable ID: p1:internal:finite-two-orientation-graph-control-exceptions. The actual finite two-orientation graph-control set and its quadratic degree/order budget are internal. Derivative signs, controlled global coverage and bounded parametrizations remain separate.

PolynomialAuxiliaryExceptions proves a finite-family Bezout theorem over every infinite field. Its actual exceptional locus consists of P=0 together with a zero of some auxiliary polynomial not divisible by P. Every finite population has size at most deg(P) times the sum of the actual auxiliary degrees, and a genuine finite set with exactly that membership is constructed. Divisible auxiliaries are omitted from this locus and proved zero on the entire actual curve. On any subset of the curve avoiding the locus, each auxiliary restriction is therefore identically zero or nowhere zero. No independence or nonzero-auxiliary premise is imposed on the family.

GraphControlPolynomials constructs the concrete two-orientation graph-control family. Its ten static polynomials are P_x, P_y, P_x+P_y, P_x-P_y, x-1, x+1, y-1, y+1, x and y. The last two retain the zeroth-order coordinate restrictions explicitly. The other 2r polynomials are the exact positive-order numerators for y as a function of x and x as a function of y, through order r, using the corrected internally proved recurrence and exact coordinate transposition. Every actual degree is at most 1+2 deg(P)(r+1), the degree sum has an explicit (10+2r) allowance, and the total Bezout budget is at most 30 deg(P)^2 (r+1)^2 for positive-degree P.

GraphControlExceptions constructs the genuine finite set for this full family at every irreducible real plane equation of positive degree. It retains exact membership and the uniform bound E.card<=30 deg(P)^2 (r+1)^2. All singular curve points are already contained in it: the internally proved actual nonzero partial of strictly smaller degree cannot be divisible by P, and its evaluation vanishes at every singular point. Thus every actual curve point outside this set is nonsingular without an additional singular exceptional allowance. Every concrete control restriction has the exact zero-or-nowhere-zero dichotomy on every subset avoiding E.

The primary BCN author version arXiv:2302.04209v2 Section 4 equations (22)-(23) and Lemma 9 were rechecked. Any later argument requiring signs through order r+1 must invoke this construction at r+1; no higher order is inferred from the order-r index range.
